articles.title: How to watch the 2026 WNBA Finals: Golden State Valkyries vs. Atlanta Dream game schedule, where to stream and more
articles.summary: Here's how to tune in to the 2026 WNBA Finals between the Golden State Valkyries and the Atlanta Dream
articles.body:
History will be made during this year's WNBA Finals , because no matter who wins, they'll be a first-time champion. The Golden State Valkyries and the Atlanta Dream both edged out past champions the Las Vegas Aces and the New York Liberty, respectively, in the semifinals to earn their spots in the best-of-seven finals series, which begins this Saturday. Game 1 will take place at the Chase Center in San Francisco; tipoff is at 3:30 p.m. ET/12:30 p.m. PT on NBC.

Here's what you need to know about the complete WNBA Finals schedule and how to watch every game.

Streaming: DirecTV , YouTube TV , Peacock and more

The WNBA Finals begin on Saturday, Oct. 17. Game 1 will begin at 3:30 p.m. ET/12:30 p.m. PT at the Chase Center in San Francisco .

Games 1 and 4 of the WNBA Finals will air on NBC. Games 2, 3, 5, 6, and 7 (if necessary) are scheduled for USA and CNBC. Every WNBA Finals game will also stream on Peacock.

Where to watch the WNBA Finals without cable

You can tune in to NBC, USA and CNBC via live TV platforms like YouTube TV, DirecTV and Fubo. Every game will also be streaming live on Peacock.

Game 1: Oct. 17, 3:30 p.m. ET, NBC and Peacock

Game 2: Oct. 19, 8 p.m. ET, Peacock, USA Network, CNBC

Game 3: Oct. 22, 8 p.m. ET, Peacock, USA Network, CNBC

articles.title: 7-foot-3 Thunder rookie faces Spanish club’s threat as OKC steps in to defend its rising star
articles.summary: Aday Mara has played five preseason games for the Oklahoma City Thunder, yet Basket Zaragoza says his contract with the Spanish club is still alive.
articles.body: Aday Mara has played five preseason games for the Oklahoma City Thunder, yet Basket Zaragoza says his contract with the Spanish club is still alive. The team said Friday it will oppose any international transfer request and is ready to go to court. Oklahoma City replied within hours, saying the NBA already told it no clearance is needed. The dispute has reached FIBA, the Spanish federation, and the league office. The Thunder appear set against paying any fee. The 7-foot-3 center is expected to play when the season opens Tuesday in San Antonio.Why is Basket Zaragoza threatening the Thunder over Aday Mara?Basket Zaragoza says its claim rests on a contract it says never ended. The club’s statement put it plainly: “The player has a contract in force for the 2026-27 season with Basket Zaragoza.” Its argument is that Aday Mara’s 2023 move to UCLA did not cancel the deal, since FIBA does not require an international transfer for players going to the NCAA. The club says it shared its stance with the Spanish federation, FIBA, the NBA and the Thunder after the draft.Zaragoza has not received any transfer request so far. If one arrives, the club says it will oppose it and go to court if needed. The Spanish side is reported to want a fee near $700,000, and Oklahoma City shows no interest in paying.The Thunder point to the college years. After three seasons in the NCAA, a team spokesperson said, “no clearance from the Spanish team is required,” as the NBA advised.Zaragoza has tried this before. When Mara agreed to play for UCLA in 2023, the club challenged the eligibility case, saying a contract was still active. It did not get the outcome it wanted.Will Aday Mara play for the Thunder this season?All signs point to yes. The No. 12 pick is expected to suit up in San Antonio on Tuesday after a preseason that drew plenty of attention. Mara averaged 13.4 points, 7.6 rebounds, 2.8 assists and 2.4 blocks over five games and made 26 of 33 shots. Some fans have started calling the rookie the “Wemby stopper,” a nod to Spurs star Victor Wembanyama.Oklahoma City lost guard Otega Oweh to a ruptured right Achilles tendon this week, and the 263-pound center could see major minutes. The rookie deal pays about $5.8 million this season, with team options on the final two years.Both the NBA and FIBA have been told about the dispute. articles.title: How many points did LeBron James score on his Philadelphia 76ers home preseason debut?
articles.summary: LeBron James has made his highly anticipated Sixers debut against the Boston Celtics.
articles.body: LeBron James has made his highly anticipated Sixers debut against the Boston Celtics. The NBA veteran scored eight points in his home preseason debut for the Philadelphia 76ers on Friday, logging 25 minutes. Further, James brought eight rebounds and seven assists. He opened with a missed three-pointer on the first possession and had to wait until midway through the first quarter for his first basket in a Sixers uniform. Joel Embiid led Philadelphia in scoring, and both Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown reached 20 points or more. Coach Nick Nurse took James out with 3:25 left in the third quarter.How did LeBron James play in his 76ers debut?Joel Embiid won the opening tip and the ball went straight to LeBron James, who missed from three. His first basket came later in the quarter off a steal. He tipped a pass from Boston’s Hayden Gray toward Maxey, sprinted ahead with no defender near him, and finished a Maxey lob with a fast-break dunk. The NBA’s all-time leading scorer was on the board.The two worked well together from there. On one possession James set a screen at the top of the key, cut to the rim and laid in a Maxey pass. On several others he brought the ball up the court himself, which took ballhandling off Maxey and let the guard move without it, either toward the basket or to the corner for open threes.By the time Nurse sent Brown in for him, James had eight points, eight rebounds, seven assists and a steal. His plus-minus of +17 was the best among the main contributors, and it came on a night when three teammates scored 20 or more.Who else stood out for the 76ers against the Celtics?Embiid led the team in scoring and went 11 of 13 at the free-throw line, moving easily on a frame reportedly 20 to 25 pounds lighter than last season. Boston was missing Mitchell Robinson and Neemias Queta, so he never had to deal with either one. Maxey backed him with 22 points and six assists on 7-of-11 shooting.Brown had his own storyline. Philadelphia acquired him from Boston in July, and Friday was his first game against the Celtics since the trade. He played 31 minutes and finished with 20 points, eight rebounds, three assists and two blocks. Jayson Tatum was not there to face, either, since Boston rested several starters, among them Robinson, Derrick White and Paul George, who went to the Celtics in the Brown deal.The Sixers’ last outing, a 144-106 loss at Boston a week earlier, had none of this. James, Embiid, Brown and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope all sat out that game.Caldwell-Pope added seven points and two assists in 21 minutes, and Jabari Walker gave the bench a boost with 13 points and four rebounds, going 4 of 8 from the field and 5 of 5 at the line. Other reserves had a harder time finding a rhythm.The regular season opens Tuesday, when Philadelphia visits the defending champion New York Knicks at Madison Square Garden. articles.title: "I feel like a pawn in the whole thing" - John Stockton got caught in Michael Jordan's Olympic money dispute
articles.summary: Jordan fought hard to honor his contract with Nike and dragged John Stockton's name along with it.
articles.body:
Months before the 1992 Olympics, some of basketball's biggest names were in danger of missing the Barcelona Games because of a dispute over money and apparel.

Michael Jordan , John Stockton and several others with Nike endorsement contracts found themselves in the middle of a disagreement with USA Basketball over the use of their likeness on merchandise.

The threat was serious enough that officials suggested the players consider withdrawing if they couldn't agree to the terms.

Jordan, the most famous name on the list, wanted an exception, while Stockton said he was willing to go to any lengths to make Dream Team inclusion possible.

Jordan and the others faced an ultimatum

In March 1992, Stockton's name suddenly appeared on paper as one of three players, all represented by David Falk, who had been given an ultimatum by USA Basketball: resign from the team or allow the organization to use their likenesses on Team USA gear. The other two were Jordan and Patrick Ewing.

As the trio's most recognizable name, MJ was also the most vocal. Several weeks before the news broke, Jordan explicitly said he wouldn't allow the federation to use his image and likeness on any apparel because he was under contract with the Swoosh.

Stockton, on the other hand, thought the "NBA precludes anything else," meaning the league could use his image however they liked. That includes any apparel with USA Basketball. Apparently, that wasn't the case.

Knowing his spot on the Dream Team was in jeopardy, Stockton did what he had to do. He talked with USAB officials and told them he would cooperate in any way necessary. The Jazz point guard revealed that if it were up to players like him, this wouldn't be a problem. But because of Nike's objections, things got more complicated.

"That's really limited things for most players," said Stockton. "But really, it was through no say of mine. From my standpoint, it's been really embarrassing. I feel like a pawn in the whole thing."

As to his conversation with USA Basketball President Dave Gavitt, Stockton clarified: " I told him I'd do anything you like. I have no intentions of doing anything that would compromise my being on the team. I said if he had any problems, come to me. I told him my position is I'd do anything they ask, short of going to court."

Ultimately, things were ironed out. Jordan's likeness would no longer be used on U.S. Olympic team basketball apparel. The agreement came in the wake of a meeting with Gavitt just a few days after Stockton told the USAB president he would do everything in his power to play on the Dream Team.

Apparently, Jordan had the same thing in mind, but the Chicago Bulls superstar also wanted to do right by Nike.

"I'm just glad that it's been settled and I can move on," Jordan said . "I wanted to relieve all the threats and the ultimatums that I was receiving. I want to play, but all this other matter didn't have anything to do with Michael Jordan. It's all with different endorsements that I have and those companies."

Jordan, Stockton, Ewing and the three other Nike athletes remained with the team. They went on to win a gold medal and became the world's ambassadors for the sport.

That said, Jordan and all the other players with shoe contracts had one final hurdle to overcome. They were handed Team USA jackets with the Reebok logo (the official USAB outfitter) for the gold medal ceremony, so how would they handle it?

Well, Jordan covered the emblem with the U.S. flag. Charles Barkley, a Nike athlete, did the same as did Magic Johnson (Converse).

"I don't believe in endorsing my competitor," Jordan said . "My contract with Nike is much more lucrative than my contract with Reebok, by far. So I wouldn't even want to show that loyalty (to Reebok)."

Jordan reportedly had a royalty deal with Nike rumored to be at five percent, so he had the monetary motive to do it. As a businessman, that makes perfect sense. Why would he be photographed with a competitor's insignia when it offered no monetary advantage?

Still, His Airness did something that let someone profit off him. After coming down off the podium during the medal ceremony, Jordan tossed the jacket aside and gave it to Brian McIntyre, the NBA public relations chief at the time.

McIntyre kept the jacket for decades and had Jordan sign it in 1994. He sold it in 2023 at a Sotheby's auction for $1.5 million. Sotheby's called the jacket "the ultimate symbol" of Jordan's loyalty to Nike.

articles.title: In 2026, a Golden State Warriors charity event raised a record $5 million for education and youth programs across the Bay Area
articles.summary: The Golden State Warriors raised more than $5 million at their annual charity poker tournament on Jan. 31, 2026.
articles.body: The Golden State Warriors raised more than $5 million at their annual charity poker tournament on Jan. 31, 2026. The fundraiser set a new record for the event and will support education and youth programmes through the Golden State Community Foundation. The tournament took place at Chase Center in San Francisco, with MGM Rewards returning as the presenting sponsor.The fundraiser also continued a recent rise in donations, topping the $3.8 million raised in 2025. The foundation will use the proceeds to support nonprofit organisations working with young people in Alameda and San Francisco counties Warriors Charity Poker Tournament breaks its fundraising recordThe 12th annual tournament raised more than the $3.8 million collected at the 2025 event. It also topped the previous record of more than $3.5 million, set in 2024. The latest result marked a new high for the Warriors' annual fundraiser.The Warriors and their community foundation host the event to raise money for the foundation's annual grants programme. Players, coaches, front-office members and foundation supporters attend the tournament. Participants can compete against Warriors players and coaches, with special prizes and experiences also part of the event.Poker brings everyone together for the evening, but the money raised serves a purpose beyond the tables. The foundation directs its grants towards nonprofits working on educational equity and youth development in Alameda and San Francisco counties.That focus gives the fundraiser a clear local purpose. The organisations supported by the foundation work with young people in communities where access to educational resources and opportunities can be limited.The foundation has confirmed the record total for 2026. However, it has not released a detailed breakdown showing how much of the tournament's proceeds each nonprofit will receive. The $5 million figure represents the amount raised for the foundation, not a confirmed payment to one school or organisation.The increase from $3.8 million in 2025 to more than $5 million in 2026 also continues the event's recent fundraising growth. The 2024 tournament raised more than $3.5 million, making the latest result the strongest of the three editions. How the foundation supports education and youthThe Golden State Community Foundation supports nonprofits that work to improve educational opportunities for young people. Its annual grants programme focuses on educational equity and youth development in Alameda and San Francisco counties.Its wider community work includes STEM education, elementary literacy, college access and other youth development programmes. These efforts support organisations that help students build academic skills and access opportunities beyond the classroom.The foundation's work covers more than one area of education. Literacy programmes help children develop reading skills, while STEM initiatives introduce students to science, technology, engineering and mathematics. College access programmes help students prepare for education after high school.The charity poker tournament raises funds for the foundation's annual grants programme, but the official event recap does not identify the specific programmes that will receive money from the 2026 proceeds. It would therefore be premature to assign part of the $5 million to a particular school, subject or nonprofit without a separate announcement.The Warriors also support youth organisations through other fundraising efforts. One example is Hoops 4 Kids, a programme that links the team's three-point shooting during the regular season to donations for local nonprofits.The foundation announced $643,000 in grants through Hoops 4 Kids in 2026. The total came from 1,286 Warriors three-pointers during the 2025-26 regular season, with each basket generating $500 for local organisations.Eight nonprofits received support through that initiative. They included the Boys and Girls Clubs of Oakland and San Francisco, East Oakland Youth Development Center, OneGoal, Playworks Northern California, Horizons at San Francisco Friends School, New Door Ventures and Scientific Adventures for Girls.The organisations serve young people in different ways. Some focus on academic support and college preparation, while others provide after-school activities, job training, play-based learning or access to science and technology.The $643,000 raised through Hoops 4 Kids is separate from the poker tournament's $5 million total. The two programmes have different fundraising structures, even though both support youth in the Bay Area.Warriors continue their community work beyond basketballThe poker tournament is one part of the Warriors' broader community efforts. The Golden State Community Foundation also works with local nonprofits through other programmes and partnerships that support education, youth development and community wellbeing.Hoops 4 Kids offers a direct link between the team's performance and charitable funding. Every made three-pointer during the relevant regular season generates $500 for the programme's beneficiaries. That approach allows the team's on-court results to contribute to community funding throughout the season rather than at a single event.The poker tournament follows a different model. It brings supporters and members of the Warriors organisation together for one annual fundraiser, with the proceeds supporting the foundation's grants programme.The recent fundraising totals show how the event has grown. It raised more than $3.5 million in 2024, reached $3.8 million in 2025 and surpassed $5 million in 2026. The latest edition established a new record for the tournament.The foundation's community work also extends beyond the amounts raised at individual events. Its grantmaking supports nonprofit organisations that work directly with students and young people. Those groups deliver programmes in local communities, where access to educational support and youth services can make a difference.The foundation has not yet published a breakdown of the 2026 poker tournament proceeds by recipient. The eventual distribution will provide a clearer picture of which organisations receive support from this year's record fundraiser.The money will support the Golden State Community Foundation's annual grants programme for nonprofits focused on educational equity and youth development in Alameda and San Francisco counties.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Ricky y Laprovittola desarman de nuevo al Barcelona
articles.standfirst: Ambos dan un recital en un partido perfecto de la Penya que vuelve a ganar al Barça
articles.summary: Ambos dan un recital en un partido perfecto de la Penya que vuelve a ganar al Barça
articles.body: El Asisa Joventut volvió a ganar al Barça, esta vez por 113-89, en el duelo correspondiente a la cuarta jornada de la Liga Endesa, tras otro recital de los bases Ricky Rubio y Nico Laprovittola, que entre ambos firmaron 36 puntos y 14 asistencias. Además de las dos estrellas verdinegras, también fue pieza clave Eli Ndiaye, que anotó 17 puntos sin ningún error en todo el encuentro. En el Barça, tan sólo Tyrese Martin fue capaz de echarse el equipo a sus espaldas con 21 puntos anotados. Los azulgranas comenzaron el derbi catalán más acertados en ataque que los verdinegros, y rápidamente ese aspecto se tradujo en el marcador tras unos buenos minutos de Martin (9-15, min. 5). Aunque el Barça siguió con acierto, el Asisa Joventut mejoró sus porcentajes con un buen Ludde Hakanson, lo que impidió que los visitantes se escaparan en el marcador (16-21, min. 8). En los minutos posteriores el Barça llegó a irse hasta diez puntos arriba, pero un buen último minuto de la Penya, con la inspiración del joven Adrián Torres de por medio, cerraron el primer cuarto con un 23-26 que no gustó a Sekulic. La dinámica era favorable para los verdinegros, y en un abrir y cerrar de ojos firmaron un parcial de 15-0 en el que Hakanson volvió a ser protagonista para provocar el tiempo muerto urgente en el conjunto azulgrana. El Asisa Joventut no bajó el ritmo en ataque y defensa, y aumentó su ventaja tras un triple de Álex Reyes, que como siempre fue un seguro desde dicha distancia (47-39, min. 18). Sin embargo, cuando parecía que los locales podían escaparse en el marcador, el Barça apretó en defensa, y volvió al ritmo anotador del inicio del partido, para poner el 49-45 al descanso. En la reanudación, el Barça intentó darle la vuelta lo antes posible a la situación, pero se topó con Ricky Rubio, que de nuevo fue clave en las jugadas ofensivas de la Penya para que mantuvieran su ventaja (57-52, min. 23). Con el encuentro igualado, al igual que pasó en el inicio del segundo cuarto, el Asisa Joventut metió la sexta marcha en el acelerador y un gran tiro de Torres puso un +10 que hizo levantar a todo el Olímpic (69-59, min. 26). Y si alguien faltaba por unirse a la fiesta era Nico Laprovittola, que en medio minuto anotó cinco puntos consecutivos para disparar a los suyos hasta la máxima y acabar el cuarto con un 82-68 que aún no era definitivo, pero sí clave para el devenir del derbi. Los azulgranas no reaccionaron en el inicio del último periodo y el Asisa Joventut lo aprovechó para seguir aumentando la ventaja gracias a los triples de Reyes y Ndiaye (93-75, min. 35). La Penya no aflojó y Laprovittola siguió con su buena versión de la segunda mitad para poner un 100-80 que sentenció definitivamente el partido a falta de tres minutos. Al final, el Asisa Joventut se llevó el derbi ante el Barça por 113-89 para sumar la segunda victoria de la temporada en la Liga Endesa y escalar hasta la zona noble de la clasificación. 113. Asisa Joventut (23+26+33+31): Rubio (19), Ellis (9), Reyes (9), Ndiaye (17), Sulejmanovic (16) -cinco inicial-; Laprovittola (17), Hakanson (10), Torres (9), Nogués (-), Birgander (4) y Cheatham (3). 89. Barça (26+19+23+21): Robinson (12), Punter (7), Parra (7), Martin (21), Balcerowski (10) -cinco inicial-; Gibson (5), Umude (9), Ubal (-), Nkamhoua (-), Núñez (-), Evbuomwan (9) y Nebo (9). Árbitros: Fernando Calatrava, Alberto Sánchez e Iyán González. Sin eliminados. Incidencias: Partido correspondiente a la cuarta jornada de la Liga Endesa de baloncesto disputado en el Palau Municipal d'Esports de Badalona ante 10.248 espectadores.

articles.title: Nuggets player who will shock NBA world with breakout 2026-27 season
articles.summary: The Denver Nuggets are coming into the 2026-27 season hoping to regain their status as one of the Western Conference’s contending teams following a disappoin...
articles.body:
The Denver Nuggets are coming into the 2026-27 season hoping to regain their status as one of the Western Conference's contending teams following a disappointing playoff flameout in the opening round against the Minnesota Timberwolves. In order to do so, the Nuggets are going to need some of the players on the back-end of their roster to potentially have a breakout season and solidify their depth.

The Nuggets have quite a few young players on the roster who could conceivably make a big impact on the team. Spencer Jones is fresh off a new contract and job security after playing the past few seasons on a two-way deal. DaRon Holmes II's rookie season was over before it began due to injury, but since then he's been unable to crack the rotation. But one player who had already shown flashes during preseason and could be a potential draft steal is rookie Trevon Brazile.

Trevon Brazile poised for Nuggets breakout season

Yes, Brazile is a rookie and thus, does not have any NBA experience. He's still a candidate for a potential breakout season considering he was passed over by every single team, some more than once, before being selected with the No. 35 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Brazile was originally drafted by the San Antonio Spurs, but had his draft rights traded to the Nuggets for Tarris Reed Jr. The idea that the Nuggets could have nabbed a steal was initially on display during NBA Summer League.

He suited up in three summer league games in Las Vegas, and averaged 18.7 points, 8.3 rebounds and 1.3 blocked shots in a little over 27 minutes. He shot 45.5 percent from the field, 47.4 percent from the 3-point line and 80 percent shooting from the free-throw line. That momentum has carried over to the preseason.

Nuggets head coach David Adelman has given Brazile regular rotation minutes during all five preseason games, and even started him in place of Aaron Gordon in the preseason finale against the Los Angeles Lakers on Oct. 16. He responded with 12 points, eight rebounds, two assists, two steals and two blocked shots while shooting 5-of-7 from the field and 2-of-3 from the 3-point line in 27 minutes.

His breakout preseason performance came just two nights prior against the LA Clippers when he finished with a team-high 22 points off the bench. He shot 8-of-10 from the field and 3-of-4 from 3-point range in team-high 25 minutes.

If this is any indication on how Brazile's game will translate to the NBA, pencil him in for one of the All-Rookie teams. And there are two key reasons as to why this is such a welcome sign for the Nuggets. One, they can afford to get Aaron Gordon some rest. And two, it helps ease the loss of Peyton Watson .

Brazile is almost built in the same mold as Gordon is. He's a versatile defensive player and good finisher in the paint. He hits the glass hard. And he's showing the ability to be a stretch-four who can consistently knock down the 3-point shot. He's also incredibly athletic on a team that has lacked youth and athleticism.

Normally, candidates for breakout seasons are players that have already been in the NBA, but for the Nuggets, it just might be a rookie for them. If Brazile does have a huge year, it would definitely be shocking for the NBA world considering every front office didn't think highly enough of him to draft him in the first round. It's likely his age and having played five seasons of college basketball played a factor. But they missed out on one of the most NBA ready rookies.

articles.title: Ben Simmons Injured, Latest Updates on Kings Star's Achilles and Status of NBA Comeback
articles.summary: Ben Simmons' NBA comeback has been halted before it could truly begin.
articles.body:
Ben Simmons' NBA comeback has been halted before it could truly begin.

The Sacramento Kings announced on Sunday that Simmons suffered a torn right Achilles. He will undergo surgery that is expected to sideline him for the entirety of the 2026-27 season.

Ben Simmons Calls Doc Rivers 'A Piece of S--t'

Simmons, 30, was having a strong preseason for the Kings after missing the entirety of the 2025-26 campaign, averaging 10.5 points, four rebounds and four assists in two games. He was expected to earn a starting position with the team ahead of Wednesday night's season-opener against the Los Angeles Clippers.

There was a lot of optimism regarding Simmons:

It's been a rough few years for Simmons from a basketball perspective.

Since forcing his way out of Philadelphia in the 2021-22 campaign, he's appeared in just 108 games over the last five years in brief stints with the Brooklyn Nets and Los Angeles Clippers. He didn't pick up with a team at all in the 2025-26 season and was away from the sport entirely, but certainly seemed excited about being back this season.

"When you have done something your whole life and so you're used to it, that is a big part of who I am," Simmons told Andscape's Marc J. Spears earlier in October. "I know what I am without it [basketball] now. But I also know it's a huge part of my life now. I'm just being grateful for being able to compete and play. And also knowing when this is done I have [another] part of my life, which is cool."

Unfortunetly, that comeback will now be put on hold for another year.

articles.title: Steph Curry Injured, Video Shows Star Limping Off at Warriors Practice Ahead of NBA Season
articles.summary: Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry suffered an ankle injury during the team's open practice on Sunday ahead of next week's season opener.
articles.body:
Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry suffered an ankle injury during the team's open practice on Sunday ahead of next week's season opener.

According to the Warriors , Curry suffered a right ankle sprain.

Curry, 38, is heading into his 18th season with the Warriors on an expiring $62 million contract.

He was available for just half of the 2025-26 campaign due to ankle, quadricep and knee injuries.

That included an issue Curry described as "runner's knee," which sidelined him for two months between February and April.

When available last season, Curry averaged 26.6 points on 46.8 percent shooting from the field and 39.3 shooting from deep.

He added 3.6 rebounds, 4.7 assists and 1.1 steals per game while playing 30.9 minutes per night in 43 games.

Curry's absence had a major impact on his team's success, especially when he missed time while Jimmy Butler was already sidelined with a knee injury.

The Warriors went 13-26 without Curry in the lineup and 24-19 with him playing. Curry ultimately returned in time for last spring's play-in tournament but was unable to will his team to victory over the Phoenix Suns.

As Butler continues recovering from the surgical repair of his torn right ACL he underwent in January, having Curry in the lineup will be crucial to the Warriors' hopes of staying in postseason contention.

Should Curry ultimately miss any time, Draymond Green could be tasked with increasing his offensive production as Brandin Podziemski and De'Anthony Melton see more playing time in the backcourt.

articles.title: Kings' Ben Simmons sustains torn Achilles tendon in practice, will undergo surgery

ESPN's Shams Charania reported that the injury is expected to be season-ending.

But if there's one thing I've learned, it's that adversity doesn't define you. How you respond to it does.

"I've been knocked down before, and I've always found a way to get back up. This time will be no different."

Simmons, whose NBA career has been heavily hampered by injuries, was hoping to make a comeback this season. He signed a one-year, $3.5 million deal with the Kings last month after going unsigned last year; previously, his last contract was with the Los Angeles Clippers in the 2024-25 season.

The 30-year-old Simmons, who was expected to be a backup point guard to rookie Darius Acuff Jr., played in all five of Sacramento's preseason games. Simmons started in the Kings' preseason loss to the San Antonio Spurs on Friday, playing 26 minutes and scoring 14 points.

articles.title: Cason Wallace, Thunder Reportedly Agree to $139M Contract Extension, Updated Salary Cap, Apron Space
articles.summary: Cason Wallace has been an important secondary contributor for the Oklahoma City Thunder throughout his career, and they made sure that won't change in the immediate future on Sunday.
articles.body:
Cason Wallace has been an important secondary contributor for the Oklahoma City Thunder throughout his career, and they made sure that won't change in the immediate future on Sunday.

Oklahoma City and the guard agreed to a five-year, $139 million rookie-scale contract extension, per ESPN's Shams Charania.

The Thunder are $51.5 million over the cap and had $6.9 million remaining in second apron space in 2026-27, per Spotrac . However, team will have a tough budget in 2027-28.

This comes after the Thunder exercised the $7.4 million club option for the 2026-27 season on his contract in October 2025. That previous move made sure he was not scheduled for restricted free agency until the summer before the 2027-28 campaign.

Now there is even more long-term certainty for the guard following this development.

And that is welcome news for the Thunder as well considering his overall importance as a role player for one of the best teams in the league.

Wallace averaged 6.8 points per game as a rookie in 2023-24 while largely coming off the bench and then saw an increase in usage in his second season. The end result was 68 regular-season appearances, 43 of which were starts, and he averaged 8.4 points, 3.4 rebounds, 2.5 assists and 1.8 steals per game while shooting 47.4 percent from the field and 35.6 percent from deep.

That was just the start of things for the Kentucky product, as he helped lead the Thunder to the championship during the 2024-25 campaign.

His ability to hit from deep plays well alongside Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, as the gravitational pull from the MVP guard often leads to open looks on the wings for his teammates. But Wallace does far more than just hit outside shots.

He is an elite defender as well and consistently guards some of the best playmakers on the opposing side.

In fact, he finished seventh in Defensive Player of the Year voting in his third season in the league in 2025-26 while averaging a career-high 8.6 points per game and connecting on 35.1 percent of his triples on the offensive end.

The Thunder finished with the best record in the league at 64-18, although they lost to the San Antonio Spurs in the Western Conference Finals even though Wallace averaged a solid 10.1 points per game in the series.

With Wallace now signed for the immediate future, he will look to continue doing his part to help the Thunder dominate the NBA and contend for more championships.

articles.title: ‘I’m Gutted for Him,’ ‘Absolutely Brutal’ — NBA World Devastated As Ben Simmons’ Highly Anticipated Comeback Gets Derailed by Achilles Tear
articles.summary: Sacramento Kings guard-forward Ben Simmons tore his right Achilles tendon during a live drill at Sunday’s practice, just three days before he was scheduled t...
articles.body:
Sacramento Kings guard-forward Ben Simmons tore his right Achilles tendon during a live drill at Sunday's practice, just three days before he was scheduled to make his official NBA comeback in Wednesday's 2026-27 regular-season opener against the Los Angeles Clippers.

ESPN's Shams Charania reported the injury on the same day the network premiered "Being Ben," an E60 documentary chronicling the former No. 1 pick's attempt to revive his career. Simmons vowed to return, while NBA personalities lamented the "devastating" news.

NBA Community Bemoans Ben Simmons' Season-Ending Achilles Injury

Shortly after Charania's report, the Kings confirmed that an MRI revealed a torn right Achilles tendon and that Simmons would undergo surgery. Charania described the season-ending injury as "a devastating turn of events on the eve of his NBA return after rehabilitating from back surgeries."

The three-time All-Star has not played more than 51 games in a season since the 2020-21 campaign with the Philadelphia 76ers and sat out the entire 2025-26 season to heal from lingering back and leg injuries.

Simmons showed he was healthy during an Australian national team minicamp in August, worked out for Kings general manager Scott Perry in Miami, and signed a one-year, $3.5 million deal in September.

In an Andscape feature tied to the documentary, published Oct. 12, he said he had not gone through all that rehabilitation only to stay off the court.

Later Sunday, the 30-year-old responded optimistically to his latest setback in a statement on Instagram: "This injury is another chapter in my journey, not the end of my story."

Simmons wrote that stepping away from the game is never easy, especially after what it took to return, and closed with a vow: "I've been knocked down before, and I've always found a way to get back up. This time will be no different."

Reactions began pouring in within minutes of Charania's post. Spotrac's Keith Smith was among the first to weigh in, writing that he was "gutted for him, especially after all the preseason buzz was so positive from him and the Kings."

Simmons appeared in two of the Kings' five exhibition outings and started both, averaging 10.5 points, 4.0 rebounds, 4.0 assists, and 0.5 steals while shooting 53.8% in 17.4 minutes per game.

"Absolutely brutal. He was back, looked like he had earned a starting job, and now this," Lakers Nation's Trevor Lane wrote.

"Extremely sad story… Simmons looked great too," NBA content creator Legend Of Winning reacted.

NBA insider Marc Stein called it "devastating in Sacramento for Ben Simmons to sustain such a serious injury just as he was about to make his official NBA comeback."

Yahoo Sports' Kevin O'Connor looked past this season, much as Simmons did in his statement: "Truly awful news. Ben Simmons had worked so hard to get back to this point. Only can hope this sets up for an even greater comeback season one year from now."

The injury also has implications for Simmons' contract. HoopsHype's Michael Scotto reported in September that his deal was non-guaranteed, but ESPN's Bobby Marks explained that the Australian will still be paid in full:

"Simmons had a $1m guarantee if he was on the roster opening day. However, because this is a significant injury (salary continuation), Simmons will receive his full salary."

Andscape's feature reported that Simmons was expected to start alongside 2026 No. 7 pick Darius Acuff Jr. in the Kings' season opener. Coach Doug Christie had praised Simmons' versatility during training camp, saying, "He can guard everybody."

Coming off a 22-60 season, tied for the worst record in the Western Conference, and a winless preseason, Sacramento will now have to find that versatility elsewhere.

Congratulations to the former Kentucky Wildcat!

articles.title: NBA tip-off: Can Timberwolves win first NBA title?
articles.summary: British-born assistant coach Tim Lewis is aiming to win the NBA title with the Minnesota Timberwolves after joining Chris Finch's staff.
articles.body:
With eight different teams the winners over the past eight seasons, it is hard to predict who takes home the NBA's Larry O'Brien Trophy in June.

If there is to be a ninth different name in as many seasons, you might look to San Antonio Spurs, with Victor Wembanyama leading the team to the Finals last season before coming unstuck against the New York Knicks.

Maybe the Philadelphia 76ers off-season moves to acquire Jaylen Brown and sign the NBA's all-time leading scorer LeBron James is an attractive pick, or perhaps the Cleveland Cavaliers.

As the season tips off, the first British-born coach in the NBA, Tim Lewis will be hoping he can assist Anthony Edwards and the Minnesota Timberwolves to their first NBA title.

Lewis has been something of a journeyman in basketball.

Born in Saint Asaph, Wales, he went on to represent the country in the 1990s, before forging a coaching career that spans almost the entire globe.

He has coached the Thailand and Qatar national teams and had spells in Germany, Belgium, Canada, the United States of America and Panama. He most recently worked in Japan as head coach of Eneos Sunflowers who he helped to the Empress Cup in January.

That is not including more than 15 years of coaching England and Great Britain age groups, where he was an assistant to now Minnesota Timberwolves head coach Chris Finch at the London 2012 Olympics.

Lewis was one of the Team GB assistant coaches, alongside Philadelphia 76ers head coach, Nick Nurse.

But Lewis and American Finch's friendship began way before that.

"We played against each other when I was back at [Crystal] Palace and Chris was at Sheffield [Sharks], he said.

"I've had stops with Chris when he was in Belgium and then before the Olympics, I spent six months at Houston with him.

"We've become close, it's almost like brothers. We've known each other 25 years and it's a strong bond."

After a previous brief spell with Minnesota, Lewis left to continue to be a head coach in Japan for three years, but Finch was persistent.

"For the last year and a half, Chris has knocked on the door and said, 'come back, come back'.

"Eventually I gave in this summer again and gone back for a more influential role, with more of an input and impact on things with stuff that's going on and I'm excited."

Lewis had a spell as a replacement coach with Minnesota's G League team, the Iowa Wolves during Covid, before joining the staff the following season with a responsibility for post-game analysis.

"I would just go through all our game plans," he told BBC Sport Wales.

"I had a little bit of player development, but it was time consuming, nobody had done it before.

"Teams do the analysis pre-game of what we're going to do and how we're going to do it with plans, but not post-game.

"I'm not sure how many of the other staff appreciated me critiquing what was going on, but that was my role, and it stayed in place."

As Lewis returns to Minnesota, his role has expanded.

"Pablo [Prigioni] is going to take the lead on the offence and my role will be to help create some of these game plans offensively," he said.

"It's a full assistant's role with responsibility for offensive game planning.

"I look at what the other team are doing defensively and what can we do to maximise our ability to beat them offensively.

"On top of that, some player development with a couple of the young bigs."

In July, Minnesota acquired Josh Green and LaMelo Ball as part of a four-team trade.

Ball scored with 272 three-point shots in the 2025-26 season, the second most of any player in the NBA.

His partnership with Anthony Edwards in the backcourt appears to be an offensive coach's dream.

"Anthony and LaMelo and those guys are going to be exciting to watch," said Lewis.

"With LaMelo, you've got somebody that can now throw the lob and Rudy becomes a bit more of a rim threat, which we haven't necessarily had.

"Teams will find it harder to double-team him when you've got people like LaMelo on the floor with him."

"I don't know whether or not Anthony wants the burden of being the next face of the NBA, who knows?

"He is an immense talent, very responsive, a great kid overall and he's a great person, very coachable and wants to get better."

It will be a daunting start for the Timberwolves this season, with Giannis Antentokounmpo and Miami Heat first up but Lewis says the team are ready for the challenge.

"We come out of the gate hard, Miami, Orlando, and then Toronto," he said.

"They've all got three bruising power forwards, which is one area where we're a bit light.

"Everybody's worried we don't have size at the four, but Chris [Finch] will figure out how that looks.

"One of the things Minnesota's going to be lucky to do is be able to play different ways and the team's going to be exciting to watch."

The ambition is clear for Minnesota and Lewis, the NBA title is the ultimate goal for 2027.

"We want to make the play-offs and get to the championship games, everybody wants to win a championship, but you've got 29 other teams that are trying to do the same thing," said Lewis.

"Fifty-plus wins a season is what you want, that puts you in a great position to make the play-offs and to be a contender for that first seed.

"You don't ever want to jinx it but everybody's saying this team has an opportunity to go a long way this year, but you never know, we've been close every year.

"Teams are going to have to adjust to the way Minnesota plays and the personnel we have."

In terms of his own predictions for the season, Lewis offered a few suggestions for potential Larry O'Brien trophy winners.

"It's one of the things about the NBA at the moment, it's somewhat unpredictable," he said.

"Teams that maybe surge in the regular season but aren't built to compete in the playoffs.

"San Antonio could be that team, Minnesota could be that team.

"We've had Denver's number now for a number of years, other than the year they won it [2023].

"Who knows what Philly's going to do with the additions they've made."

Lewis says an NBA title would mean "so much" to Minneapolis.

The franchise formed in 1989 as an expansion team, with the supporters patiently waiting to make it to the NBA Finals.

"Minnesota fans are unbelievable," he said.

"It goes way back to Minneapolis Lakers [1947-1960] that are now the Los Angeles Lakers, who did win a championship.

"As an organisation, being able to win in that environment against a bigger market team is always a huge success.

"It's more for the city, it would be an amazing accomplishment."

articles.title: Lakers Home Opener Prices Drop Without LeBron James
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers are already seeing cheaper tickets for home games after losing LeBron James. A study was done comparing all team’s lowest “get in” pri...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers are already seeing cheaper tickets for home games after losing LeBron James. A study was done comparing all team's lowest "get in" price for home openers across the NBA this season. The Lakers have typically been one of the top two most expensive teams with the New York Knicks. However, this season sees them dropping behind LeBron's new team.

Each of the top five most expensive home openers this season:

Knicks: $1,112 Boston Celtics : $160 Philadelphia 76ers : $145 San Antonio Spurs : $124 Lakers: $116

The Knicks are in a different tier since New York fans always more, and the franchise will be raising the NBA Championship banner for the first time in over five decades. Spurs fans are also paying more for the Western Conference Championship banner and an intense game vs the Oklahoma City Thunder .

The Celtics and Lakers always have higher opening night prices due to their legacy standard of a passionate fan base. However, the Lakers have fallen behind the 76ers. Fans are excited to see the first game of LeBron and Jaylen Brown in Philadelphia. Outside of these five teams, every other NBA home opener has a "get in" price under $100 to make it more affordable.

Why Lakers Prices Have Fallen Without LeBron James

The appeal of LeBron adds multiple layers for why those prices has higher value. Outside of being an all-time great, James only has so many seasons left in his 30s. The Lakers still have superstar Luka Doncic to make prices high, but he has another decade and change left in the league.

Fans pay more for LeBron games since it's a rare attraction of an iconic NBA star before he retires over the next few years. Doncic and Austin Reaves will still make the Lakers a top live NBA attraction, but other teams have stronger draws.

Victor Wembanyama is already making Spurs tickets more expensive than the Tim Duncan era when they dominated every season. The Knicks will remain the top draw since fans are ecstatic about being the class of the NBA in a market where live events are quite costly even without the context.

One could argue the Lakers lost some value without LeBron, but this is only good for the fan base. The era of James teaming with Anthony Davis and then Luka made Lakers tickets extremely expensive as one of the hottest tickets in sports.

Lakers fans priced out of games will have a better chance now and will still get to see a future Hall of Famer. Head coach JJ Redick believes the team will win games and contend this season, so that could see prices increasing throughout the season.

Regardless, the Lakers have an exciting scenario and will have less intense following than the LeBron era. Doncic has a chance to write his own legacy for the Lakers, and fans will be on board. Even the road prices have dropped for the Lakers to see fans in other cities having a chance to see them without paying a crazy price.

articles.title: A’ja Wilson cried in her coach’s arms after a playoff loss. The moment revealed her own superpower
articles.summary: This story is part of Peak, The Athletic’s desk covering the mental side of sports. Sign up for Peak’s newsletter here. Tanisha Wright coached A’ja Wilson, a...
articles.body:
This story is part of Peak, The Athletic's desk covering the mental side of sports. Sign up for Peak's newsletter here .

Tanisha Wright coached A'ja Wilson, a five-time WNBA MVP, for two seasons as an assistant with the Las Vegas Aces. She is now the head coach of Penn State.

In 2021, when I was an assistant with the Las Vegas Aces, we lost in the semifinals against the Phoenix Mercury. We were clearly the heavy favorite to win that series and return to the WNBA championship.

As we were coming off the court, A'ja Wilson cried in my arms. I was shocked because I hadn't witnessed something like that before. Not just from her, but from someone of her caliber.

A'ja is clearly a superstar, but she understood what had happened. We were the higher seed. We made the Finals the year before and then we came back with an even better team. She took that all to heart, and she took the loss that hard. She cared that much. Her emotions were so raw.

And to me, that is her superpower: She cares. And she cares about every single aspect, not just on the court.

After that loss to Phoenix, she went to a different level. A completely different level. The jump she made in one single offseason was incredible to watch from afar. That's what I learned about her because of that loss: how devoted and committed she was to living up to her greatness.

She has such a deep care for how she approaches the game, how the team is, the whole experience. It translates to everything she does: her care for the game, her care for attention to detail, her care for her own growth and the growth of the game.

It shows up every day in her work. If you have a deep love and a deep care for what you're doing, then it shows up in how you show up every single day for yourself, for your teammates, for your coaches, for your community. That translates to her success on the court.

You can't do what she's done without being present, without having your feet exactly where they are. If you don't have that level of attentiveness, it's hard to show up every single day and be as great as A'ja is.

I started coaching with the Aces in 2020. You kind of think: Here's this budding superstar . We were in the bubble that year, and I started noticing that about her the minute I showed up.

I used to describe her this way: She's the right kind of superstar. She checks every single box.

She wanted to be coached. Here I was, a first-time WNBA assistant coach, and I ran a lot of our practices. I'd tell her: A'ja, you need to run harder .

Her response would be: OK, I got you, T .

It might seem overly simple, like there should be more, but that's just who she was.

It didn't matter if you were a first-time coach or a former player. You could laugh with her and talk trash to her. She set the tone for the team every single day.

And she did it because she cared so much about everything.

There's an air of excitement surrounding the Chicago Bulls this upcoming season.

The Bulls will open the 2026-27 campaign on October 21 against the Toronto Raptors at Scotiabank Arena in Canada.

They might not be playoff contenders just yet, but Josh Giddey is feeling pretty confident and excited about the team.

GettyJosh Giddey #3 of the Chicago Bulls looks on against the Boston Celtics at the United Center on November 29, 2024 in Chicago, Illinois.

Speaking to Joe Cowley of the Chicago Sun-Times , Josh Giddey expressed his excitement about playing with athletic, above-the-rim players for the first time in his career.

Giddey feels confident that anytime he throws a lob next season, it'll be caught and finished with ease.

"I feel like I can throw pretty much every pass, and lobs are just one that I've never really had to throw a lot in my career," Giddey said.

"Whether it's wings or our fives, we've got guys that can catch lobs all around," he added. "I've got to get better at throwing them, but I think it's going to be good to have guys that I can kind of put it anywhere around the cylinder and they'll go take care of the rest."

The 24-year-old Australian star is alluding to fellow young players like Matas Buzelis and Caleb Wilson , who will be the starting forwards. Nic Claxton is also capable of catching lobs at center, so it's going to be a pretty fun season in Chicago.

Giddey has been working with his new teammates, Wilson and Claxton, this offseason. But his partnership with Claxton will have to wait since the big man is dealing with an injury and won't be available on opening night.

Giddey Ranked 84th in Top 100 NBA Players List

In his second season in Chicago, Josh Giddey had a breakout campaign. He averaged 17.0 points, 8.3 rebounds, 9.1 assists and 1.0 steals per game.

Giddey was on track to be an All-Star before getting hit with an injury to start the new calendar year. He ended up playing just 54 games as the Bulls stumbled with a 31-51 record.

Following his career campaign, The Ringer has named Giddey as the 84th-best player in the NBA. The narrative surrounding him is whether he's capable of being a winning player or not.

"The Bulls' present and future belong to Caleb Wilson and Matas Buzelis, so this entire season is an opportunity to see who and what makes sense around them," The Ringer wrote. "Will Giddey accentuate Chicago's two most important players? … Even though he tied Jalen Johnson for the second-most triple-doubles last season, Giddey's winning impact wasn't there."

While there's no pressure on Chicago to win this season, it's a test for Giddey and how he'd fare with better players around him.

articles.title: Thunder, Cason Wallace reportedly beat deadline, agree to 5-year, $139M contract extension
articles.summary: Cason Wallace and the Oklahoma City Thunder have agreed to a five-year, $139 million extension to his rookie contract, ESPN's Shams Charania reports.
articles.body:
Cason Wallace and the Oklahoma City Thunder have agreed to a five-year, $139 million extension to his rookie contract, ESPN's Shams Charania reports .

The two sides beat Monday's deadline for players from the 2023 NBA Draft class to sign rookie scale extensions. Had they not reached a deal before the deadline, Wallace would have played the final year of his rookie contract on a team option, then entered the 2026-27 offseason as a restricted free agent.

With the deal, the Thunder secure a defensive anchor of their core as they seek to win a second NBA championship in three seasons. Wallace, a shooting guard, has developed into one of the best perimeter defenders in the NBA.

The Thunder selected Wallace with the No. 10 overall draft pick in 2023 out of Kentucky. He's expanded his role with the franchise in each of his three NBA seasons.

After starting 13 games as a rookie, Wallace started 43 in 2024-25 and was a key rotation player on Oklahoma City's championship team. He started 58 games last season and is now projected as a full-time starter this upcoming season, when he should expand on his 26.6 minutes per game from 2025-26.

In 77 games last season, Wallace averaged 8.6 points, 3.1 rebounds, 2.6 assists, 1.9 steals and 0.4 blocks while shooting 35.1% on 3.7 3-point attempts per game.

The Thunder traded 3-and-D specialist Luguentz Dort to the Atlanta Hawks in the offseason, signaling their expectation that Wallace would step into a larger role. They've now secured his services for five more seasons and signed their entire starting five to long-term contracts.

With their championship window open, the Thunder will move forward with Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Jalen Williams, Chet Holmgren, Isaiah Hartenstein and now Wallace, signed through at least the 2028-29 season.

Later that evening, Brown joins up with LeBron James, Joel Embiid, and the rest of his new Philadelphia 76ers team-mates as they travel to Madison Square Garden to face the reigning champion New York Knicks.

The slate ends with yet another fascinating match-up: a rematch of last year's seven-game epic Western Conference Finals series between reigning MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's Oklahoma City Thunder and Victor Wembanyama's San Antonio Spurs.
