articles.title: Jaylen Brown, Ja Morant and NBA Stars with Most on the Line This Season
articles.summary: Not every NBA superstar will face the same stakes as the 2026-27 season unfolds.
articles.body:
Not every NBA superstar will face the same stakes as the 2026-27 season unfolds.

The end goal is technically the same for everyone: win a championship. For a handful of big names, though, this is a mandatory opportunity to debunk misconceptions, rewrite reputations and even prevent their teams from moving in a different direction.

Using this criteria will take us beyond rote superstar expectations. Bigwigs like Giannis Antetokounmpo, Nikola Jokić, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Victor Wembanyama aren't facing any more pressure than usual. And even if they are, the uptick doesn't threaten their immediate standing among the league's top players.

The same cannot be said for the names that follow.

From Thanksgiving onward last season, the Charlotte Hornets went 40-25 while posting a top-four offense and defense . Their 44 total wins were the franchise's most since 2015-16. Despite failing to make it out of the play-in tournament, they were a trendy pick to supercharge their position over the summer and climb up the Eastern Conference pecking order.

Instead, the Hornets traded LaMelo Ball for a package that guarantees them only one outright first-round pick. Talk about sending a message.

The onus is now on LaMelo to prove Charlotte—and anyone who applauded the trade—wrong. Availability is part of the equation. If LaMelo plays in 65 contests this season, it'll be only the third time in his career. He also needs to show his ankles don't require meticulous minutes caps.

Beyond that, he'll need to prove he can drive winning as a co-star within a larger ecosystem. While he had a transcendent impact on Charlotte's offense, bare-bones roster constructions gave him carte blanche. There won't be room for as much unchecked freelancing with the Minnesota Timberwolves.

Head coach Chris Finch already talked to LaMelo about recalibrating his shot selection. Anthony Edwards has referred his new teammate to a personal driver. There is a plan in place to ensure he holds up against the physicality of playoff defenses.

Fair or not, LaMelo is portrayed as an unserious player. This can be the season he invalidates that perception—or confirms it.

Paolo Banchero is entering the most important season of his career. He still carries the burden of a No. 1 overall pick, but the pressure meter cranks to 11-out-of-10 now that he's beginning a five-year max deal and the Orlando Magic have changed their head coach.

Plenty of people behind keyboards and cameras have already written off Banchero as an inefficient ball-stopper incapable of change. The 24-year-old has turned in enough promising stretches and big playoff moments to paint the bleakest projections as over the top. But the skepticism itself is fair.

Banchero takes too many mid-range jumpers for someone who's never knocked them down at a league-average clip. Failing to clear 35 percent from three for an entire season remains a red flag when measured against his "meh" volume. Though he's made strides to shed the "ball-stopper" label, the Magic have seen their transition frequency off live rebounds plummet the past two seasons with him on the floor.

Surrounding injuries and ecosystem play a part in Banchero's perceived shortcomings. Orlando also borderline dominated the minutes he logged with Franz Wagner last year. But excuses and flashes, however viable, only get you so far.

More heads will roll if the Magic aren't firmly in the East's top six entering the trade deadline or peter out in the playoffs. No one would technically be safe in the quest for wholesale change, but Banchero's name will be the first to come up should things go awry.

Jaylen Brown's stock should technically be at an all-time high. He finished sixth in MVP voting last year en route to an All-NBA Second Team selection. The Boston Celtics also won 56 games with him as their No. 1 option while Jayson Tatum missed most of the season recovering from an Achilles injury.

And yet, Brown was still flipped over the summer for someone roughly seven years older and the promise of one additional first-round pick. Unless you think Boston is in the business of accepting actively worse offers, this return doesn't reflect well on the five-time All-Star's standing in the league.

Factoring in other forces at play —length of contract, desire for an extension, on- and off-court synergy with Jayson Tatum—doesn't diminish the burden of proof suddenly thrust upon Brown's shoulders. If anything, it increases the weight of the stigmas he's tasked with shedding.

On-off splits aren't even the beginning . The idea that Brown was the Celtics' seventh-best player is pure fiction. But Boston treated him as some combination of a net-negative asset, overpaid and addition-by-subtraction.

Can Brown be more efficient? Can he effectively scale down on a Philadelphia 76ers team with plenty of other mouths to feed? Is there more playmaking to extract out of him? A better assist-to-turnover ratio? Can he be content as something less than the unchallenged No. 1 or No. 2 option? The answers won't just determine what his next contract looks like, but whether the Sixers should be the ones giving it to him.

The Cleveland Cavaliers have always needed Evan Mobley to become their best player for their championship stock to have the proper oomph. Though he appeared well on his way to actualizing that vision in 2024-25, last year's performance was a clear step back.

Little to no notes must be given on defense. But Mobley's scoring aggression continues to wax and wane. His usage rate actually dropped from 2024-25 to last season, and he's yet to make the table-setting leap everyone's been waiting on.

Acquiring someone as heliocentric as James Harden is treated as an indictment of Donovan Mitchell's own playmaking limitations . It's also a nod to the Cavs' lack of faith in Mobley as a frontcourt creator.

We can quibble over how he's used, the state of his handle, the purpose of his touches, and his three-point shooting. He has made strides almost everywhere. The fact is, Cleveland has moved beyond needing incremental offensive improvement.

Mitchell received a max extension despite his flaws. Harden is entering his age-37 season. More than ever, the Cavs need Mobley to juice his offensive volume—not merely as a self-starter, but as more of an overall scoring constant. If that's not in the cards, Cleveland's entire trajectory changes. His future with the team might even, too.

Everything is apparently going swimmingly with the Portland Trail Blazers for Ja Morant, the teammate. It remains to be seen how Ja Morant, the basketball player, will fit once the games start to matter.

Even with the Shaedon Sharpe injury, Portland remains overloaded with guards, and Morant's play style isn't historically adaptable. He has never cut with enough frequency to be used off the ball and has not ranked higher than the 31st percentile in catch-and-shoot three-point efficiency since he was a rookie, according to BBall Index.

Expecting Deni Avdija, Damian Lillard, Scoot Henderson and Jrue Holiday to make a lion's share of the adjustments is tenuous under the best circumstances. It becomes malpractice if Morant no longer has the star power strong enough to warrant adapting around.

His rim frequency and free-throw-attempt rate have both been on the downswing since 2022. That's typically a harbinger of athletic decline. Meanwhile, if he is eating into minutes for Henderson or Holiday, it puts the Blazers at risk of a steep defensive drop-off.

It'd be a stretch to say that Morant's career hangs in the balance. But his active stardom and ability to be known as someone who can work in different situations absolutely do.

Three years into their partnership, the jury remains out on whether Alperen Şengün and Amen Thompson can work as a primary offensive tandem. This season feels like the last chance the Houston Rockets will get to validate proof of concept before having to choose between the two.

We already know who they'll pick if it comes to that.

Despite having the more limited offensive arsenal, Thompson is viewed as Houston's primary building block. That puts the onus on Şengün to adapt around him. Granted, his track record does the same.

Şengün has at least provided glimpses into potential floor-spacing. Thompson has never once looked like a jump-shooter defenses will respect. It's unrealistic to expect that will change. Even if he takes more threes and makes them at a 37 percent clip, defenses are unlikely to think twice about going under on screens or entirely sagging off him.

Houston's numbers with Şengün and Thompson on the floor don't portray this as an urgent decision. But the offense has cratered in each of the past two postseasons during their tandem minutes. And the first-chance scoring with both on the court has never been great.

Something has to change. Better yet, someone has to change. If it isn't Şengün, odds are he'll find himself on the chopping block.

Dan Favale is a National NBA Writer for Bleacher Report. Follow him on Bluesky ( @danfavale ), and subscribe to the Hardwood Knocks podcast, co-hosted by Bleacher Report's Grant Hughes .

articles.title: Final Win-Loss Record Predictions for Every NBA Team
articles.summary: On the eve of the 2026-27 NBA campaign, and after an offseason jam-packed with player movement, it's time to assess everything that's happened since the NBA Finals and predict each team's win total this season.
articles.body:
On the eve of the 2026-27 NBA campaign, and after an offseason jam-packed with player movement, it's time to assess everything that's happened since the NBA Finals and predict each team's win total this season.

We'll look at past performance and future projections. We'll also review schedules and win totals from FanDuel Sportsbook . With all of the above and a healthy dose of subjectivity, we'll be able to predict everyone's final record.

Before we get to each squad, though, there's an important note. Each NBA season has a finite number of wins and losses. There are 1,230 wins (and 1,230 losses) in total. The predictions for all 30 teams have to add up to those totals.

Our predictions do exactly that. With the housekeeping out of the way, it's time to dive into each team.

Rookies: Kingston Flemings, Zuby Ejiofor, Henri Veesaar

After finishing eighth in points allowed per 100 possessions last season, the Atlanta Hawks leaned even harder into a defense-first identity this offseason.

Luguentz Dort and Aaron Wiggins are coming over from one of the strongest defensive ecosystems in basketball to join a roster that already features Jalen Johnson, Dyson Daniels, Nickeil Alexander-Walker and Onyeka Okongwu.

This rotation has tons of length and athleticism. If it can get enough offense from Johnson, CJ McCollum and NAW, the Hawks could push for 50 wins.

In: Mike Conley, Paul George, Mitchell Robinson

Rookies: Chris Cenac Jr., Dillon Mitchell

The Boston Celtics were widely panned in the aftermath of the Jaylen Brown trade, but you don't have to look far to see why.

Paul George's contract is a year shorter than Brown's. He's more adept at playing off the ball. He also came with multiple draft picks.

The deal made Boston more financially flexible and made it easier to build the offense around Jayson Tatum.

Speaking of whom, Tatum is a better individual player than Brown, who led this core to 56 wins last season. Though George is past his prime, he should be able to provide more than Tatum did in 16 appearances in 2025-26.

With those two, Payton Pritchard, Derrick White, Mitchell Robinson and multiple developing youngsters, this team could finish first in the East.

In: Keon Ellis, Julius Randle, Moritz Wagner

Rookies: Mikel Brown Jr., Joshua Jefferson, Tyler Bilodeau

This feels a little light for a team with Julius Randle and Michael Porter Jr. The former's shooting should complement the latter's shooting well.

If Egor Dëmin, Mikel Brown or one of the other younger players on the roster performs better than expected, the Brooklyn Nets could be too.

The East is significantly stronger than it's been in the past. To limit ourselves to 1,230 total wins for the exercise, some teams will fail to reach their over/under.

In: Grayson Allen, Royce O'Neale, Naz Reid

Out: LaMelo Ball, Miles Bridges, Josh Green

Rookies: Hannes Steinbach, Christian Anderson

The Charlotte Hornets were one of the NBA's most exciting young teams last season. But a few months after their late-season surge fell shy of the playoffs, they unloaded the playmaker largely responsible for their offense.

Despite losing LaMelo Ball, it's easy to be excited about this team's future.

The Hornets still have a ton of shooting on the roster, with Kon Knueppel, Coby White, Brandon Miller paired with newcomers Grayson Allen, Royce O'Neale and Naz Reid. They're going to be able to "game the system" in a bunch of contests by simply pouring in threes.

Though the absence of LaMelo's playmaking will be felt, that trade will also give Miller and Knueppel more on-ball opportunities (and thus, more growth).

Out: Anfernee Simons, Mouhamadou Gueye, Collin Sexton

For the first time in years, it feels like there's some legitimate longterm hope for the Chicago Bulls. You don't have to look any further than the forward spots to find it.

Norman Powell and Nic Claxton should add some veteran credibility to the team. With those two, Josh Giddey now has more reliable finishers to set up. But it's Matas Buzelis and rookie Caleb Wilson who could have an impact that lasts well beyond 2026-27.

After nearly doubling his scoring average to 16.3 points last season, Buzelis looks poised to clear 20 per game in this one. Wilson, who was mostly used like a bouncy, old-school big man at North Carolina, has flashed wing skills in Summer League and the preseason.

Those two give Chicago loads of athleticism and upside.

Out: Larry Nance Jr., Keon Ellis, Dean Wade

LeBron James is obviously still a better player than Peyton Watson in a vacuum, but missing out on the legend and "settling" for Watson could ultimately prove beneficial.

Watson looks like a near-ideal complementary wing to slot between offense-first backcourt of James Harden and Donovan Mitchell and the defense-first frontcourt of Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen. He can help both duos.

On one end, Watson has developed into a reliable catch-and-shoot option and showed one-on-one scoring prowess when Nikola Jokić was out last season. On the other, he's one of the most dynamic weak-side shot-blockers in the league and a capable on-ball defender against longer wings.

Cleveland may have been swept in the conference finals, but the addition of Watson gives them one of the most complete starting fives in the league. That overall talent gives the Cavs a real shot at making the NBA Finals.

In: Santi Aldama, Tarik Biberović, Zaccharie Risacher, Marcus Sasser, Kyrie Irving (back from injury)

Out: Marvin Bagley, AJ Johnson, Khris Middleton, Ryan Nembhard

Rookies: Morez Johnson, Sergio de Larrea, Tobi Lawal, Vsevolod Ishchenko

Legitimate superstardom could come earlier than expected for Cooper Flagg, who's scoring with ease in the preseason and now has Kyrie Irving to draw defenses away.

When both are on the floor and surrounded by at least a couple of shooters, the Mavs should be tough to defend. Assuming Dereck Lively II can get healthy or Daniel Gafford can stay that way, there's plenty of length to be disruptive on the other end, too.

There's still a chance Irving is moved on from for a rebuild-eyed move. There's enough unproven talent around to make 50 wins a long shot. But 33.5 feels awfully low for the Mavs.

In: DeMar DeRozan, Marvin Bagley III, Alpha Diallo, Ryan Nembhard

Out: Tim Hardaway Jr., Jonas Valančiūnas, Bruce Brown, Peyton Watson

After another embarrassing playoff exit at the hands of the Minnesota Timberwolves, the Denver Nuggets ran it back with the same starting five, but they almost completely overhauled their second unit.

They can now run out lineups led (at least on the offensive end) by DeMar DeRozan, who should be able to light up reserve defenders. Marvin Bagley is a bouncier athlete than Jonas Valančiūnas. Though Diallo is still unproven at this level, the reigning EuroLeague Defensive Player of the Year looks more than ready to bring some chaos based on his preseason minutes.

If the starters remain a dominant regular-season force (as they should) and the new bench can simply play even with their opponents, 50 wins may be an overly conservative estimate for Denver.

In: John Collins, Isaiah Joe, Taurean Prince

Out: Tobias Harris, Caris LeVert, Marcus Sasser, Isaiah Stewart

The contract standoff between the Detroit Pistons and Jalen Duren ended with the big man signing a five-year, $200 million deal, but his return certainly doesn't guarantee a repeat of last season's success.

60 wins will be an incredibly hard total to reach this season, with the new anti-tanking rules in place and the East, specifically, taking on a ton of talent this offseason.

Even if Ausar Thompson and Cade Cunningham improve, John Collins plays better than Tobias Harris and Isaiah Joe's shooting charges up the offense (all pretty likely), there's just too much competition now for the Pistons to improve on their 2025-26 win total.

Yaxel Lendeborg looks ready to contribute to winning basketball right now. This preseason, he's averaging 23.9 points, 15.2 rebounds and 6.0 assists per 75 possessions, while shooting 44.4 percent from deep.

He could, realistically, be Golden State's second-best player right now.

But as cool as that is for him individually, it's not a formula for getting Stephen Curry back to title contention.

As good as those two might be, and as many wide-ranging contributions as Draymond Green and Brandin Podziemski might provide, the Warriors missing Jimmy Butler, Moses Moody and Kristaps Porziņģis (who remains out with a mystery illness) will be too much for those left standing to overcome.

In: Bogdan Bogdanović, Marcus Smart, Fred VanVleet (back from injury)

The Houston Rockets feel like a sneaky title contender, with Fred VanVleet returning to steady the offense and Reed Sheppard, Amen Thompson, Jabari Smith and Alperen Şengün still developing.

This rotation is suddenly loaded with playmaking (from Şengün, Sheppard, VanVleet and Thompson), shooting (from VanVleet, Kevin Durant and Sheppard, at the very least) and length (with KD, Smith and Tari Eason). Şengün and Steven Adams can make this team a nightmare on the boards again.

Beyond all that, Houston got deeper by adding veterans Bogdan Bogdanović and Marcus Smart to the second unit.

In: Larry Nance Jr., Kelly Oubre Jr., Tyrese Haliburton (back from injury)

There's a chance Tyrese Haliburton is returning to a better team than the one he left.

Andrew Nembhard and Jarace Walker had the chance to carry more responsibility in his absence. They grew because of it. Ivica Zubac doesn't shoot like Myles Turner, but he's a far better rebounder, takes up more space on defense and can be a dominant finisher inside. Kelly Oubre can replace a lot of the scoring punch Bennedict Mathurin brought off the bench.

But ultimately, the Indiana Pacers' chance of recapturing the magic of 2025 rests in the hands of Haliburton, as he's moving well in the preseason, converting jumpers and lifting everyone with his playmaking.

In: Rui Hachimura, Gradey Dick, Brandon Ingram

Out: Bogdan Bogdanović, John Collins, Kawhi Leonard

Rookies: Keaton Wagler, Baba Miller, Nick Martinelli, Narcisse Ngoy

After the NBA determined that the Los Angeles Clippers circumvented the salary cap with numerous side deals for Kawhi Leonard, the team was hit with the stiffest penalties the league has ever handed down.

While that mostly impacts the long-term prospects of the team (they have to forfeit five first-round picks), the present is pretty bleak too.

Darius Garland is a fun playmaker, but he's often hurt. Rui Hachimura has long deserved more usage on the offensive end, but it remains to be seen if he's as good a shooter without LeBron James or Luka Dončić setting him up. Brandon Ingram was hurt coming into this season. Max Strus joined him on the injury report this preseason.

Altogether, it's starting to look like the pain of this offseason was only the beginning for Clippers fans. There's a real chance this is the West's worst team right now.

In: Matisse Thybulle, Ziaire Williams, Quentin Grimes, Jaden Hardy, Walker Kessler, Kevon Looney, Sandro Mamukelashvili, Collin Sexton

Out: Rui Hachimura, Deandre Ayton, Jaxson Hayes, LeBron James, Luke Kennard, Marcus Smart

The Los Angeles Lakers may not get a ton of stops this season, but neither will their opponents.

This has been Luka Dončić's team from the moment he arrived, but now that LeBron James is gone, it's unquestionably so. He's surrounded by players who are almost entirely complementary to his game.

Walker Kessler may exemplify that most, with his rim-running and lob-catching on one end and his ability to cover for Luka and Austin Reaves' weaknesses on the other.

In: Jerami Grant, AJ Johnson, Kris Murray, Quinten Post, Isaiah Stewart

Rookies: Cameron Boozer, Karim López, Richie Saunders

It's tempting to have the Memphis Grizzlies even further clear of that over-under.

Cameron Boozer already looks like a five-year vet. In limited appearances, Ty Jerome ranked eighth in the league in estimated plus-minus last season. Zach Edey is a double-double machine when healthy.

Cedric Coward, Jaylen Wells, Cam Spencer, Scotty Pippen, Jerami Grant and Isaiah Stewart all have the potential to be quality role players in 2026-27.

This is a deep team that will play hard and be well-coached. The top-end talent still needs time to develop, but the Grizzlies will be a tougher out than many expect.

In: Giannis Antetokounmpo, Tim Hardaway Jr., Bobby Portis

Out: Tyler Herro, Kasparas Jakučionis, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Norman Powell, Kel'el Ware

There was a lot of talk of the stylistic overlap between Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo shortly after the Miami Heat traded for the former. Yes, the lack of three-point shooting from those two is a concern worth addressing.

But it's hard to look at the rest of Miami's offseason (and the resulting roster) without thinking they did exactly that.

Davion Mitchell, Klay Thompson, Andrew Wiggins, Tim Hardaway Jr. and Bobby Porter can all be plus three-point shooters, relative to their roles and positions. Pelle Larsson, Nikola Jović and Simone Fontecchio can too.

In fact, there's a world where Bam and Giannis are the only non-shooters meaningfully in the rotation. If that's the case, both should have plenty of driving lanes to exploit. The wins will stack up because of it.

In: Tyler Herro, Kasparas Jakučionis, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Caris LeVert, Kel'el Ware

Out: Giannis Antetokounmpo, Gary Harris, Bobby Portis, Taurean Prince

Rookies: Brayden Burries, Nate Ament, Malique Lewis

After years of teasing his desire to leave, the Milwaukee Bucks' Giannis Antetokounmpo era is mercifully over.

While the start of a rebuild can be painful, Bucks fans may find some solace in knowing their best player no longer has one foot out the door.

They also have a handful of intriguing young (or youngish) talents who could actually generate some hope for the future. Tyler Herro, Kasparas Jakučionis, Jaime Jaquez Jr. and rookie Brayden Burries bring loads of talent (or at least potential) on the playmaking and positional versatility fronts.

Out: Kyle Anderson, Mike Conley, Julius Randle, Naz Reid

Rookies: Isaiah Evans, Trey Kaufman-Renn

Minutes are always limited in the preseason. They'll surely need a bit of an adjustment period early in the regular season. But LaMelo Ball and Anthony Edwards have already had moments of dynamism that make it easy to get excited about the Minnesota Timberwolves' offense.

It's hard to attribute that to anything but the infusion of life that came with Ball.

"He's always in a great mood," head coach Chris Finch told reporters. "We referred to ourselves as a moody team in the last couple of years, at times, and it's probably gotten in our way. We've traded moodiness for giddiness."

With a little more joy on one end and Rudy Gobert and Jaden McDaniels still generating intensity on the other, Minnesota should be a very real title contender this season.

For years, it's felt like the New Orleans Pelicans should be talented enough to at least push for a play-in spot, but they weren't even close in each of the last two campaigns.

Despite the roster still featuring a decent amount of raw talent, the preseason over-under has clearly adjusted to their inability to meet expectations.

Still, this feels like an "if they stay healthy" play-in contender with multiple 20-point-per-game scorers (Zion Williamson, Trey Murphy III and Dejounte Murray), a pair of intriguing young talents (Derik Queen and Jeremiah Fears) and some scoring punch off the bench (Bennedict Mathurin).

It's just that the qualifier is even more loaded here than it is for other teams, considering the fact that Zion has averaged fewer than 40 appearances per year in his career.

Coming off their first title since 1973, the New York Knicks lost rebounding force Mitchell Robinson, but they're still very real contenders to finish first in the East and become the league's first repeat champs in nearly a decade.

Most importantly, they're bringing back all of their stacked starting five, with Jalen Brunson and Karl-Anthony Towns providing plenty of offense, OG Anunoby and Mikal Bridges forming one of the best three-and-D duos in the league and Josh Hart filling the few gaps that might be left after those four.

While losing Robinson could be a problem, New York still has one of the league's better backup 5s in veteran Andre Drummond.

It's not the deepest team in the East, but 50-plus wins is still very much in play.

Out: Branden Carlson, Luguentz Dort, Isaiah Joe, Aaron Wiggins

Rookies: Aday Mara, Bennett Stirtz, Otega Oweh

Going "under" on the Oklahoma City Thunder has more to do with the rest of the league than it does with OKC.

Spoiler alert: If every one of these predictions were spot-on correct, the Thunder would have the best record in the league in 2026-27.

It's easy to see everyone's win totals suppressed a bit by the new anti-tanking rules and the way talent has been spread across the NBA.

OKC contributed to the latter by unloading Luguentz Dort, Aaron Wiggins and Isaiah Joe, all in an effort to dodge the second apron. Now, their depth relies heavily on younger players like Jared McCain, Cason Wallace, Nikola Topić, Thomas Sorber and maybe even rookies Aday Mara and Bennett Stirtz.

Those two, specifically, are generating plenty of hope for the second unit. In the preseason, Mara is averaging 15.3 points, 7.3 rebounds and 3.0 assists in just 23.8 minutes, shooting 79.3 percent from the field. Stirtz has produced 17.0 points and 3.3 assists, while shooting 53.8 percent from deep.

The Orlando Magic are mostly relying on a new-coach bump to improve on last season's shy-of-expectations performance. Well, that and, hopefully, better health for their best players.

In each of the last two seasons, Franz Wagner and Jalen Suggs each missed at least 20 games. In 2024-25, Paolo Banchero missed more than 30 games.

But in that same two-year stretch, when all three of those players are on the floor, Orlando is plus-9.0 points per 100 possessions.

In: Anfernee Simons, Jaylen Brown, Ariel Hukporti, LeBron James, Dean Wade

Out: Paul George, Quentin Grimes, Kelly Oubre Jr., Andre Drummond

The questions about availability are very real for the Philadelphia 76ers.

LeBron James is entering his age-42 season. The oft-injured Joel Embiid could barely get off the floor in his lone preseason appearance. When one or both are out, the offense could bog down. Absences from either or both could also make it tough for the whole team to develop the chemistry necessary to contend.

But in terms of raw talent, there may not be another team in the league that has more in its starting five.

The aforementioned superstars, Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown and VJ Edgecombe, will bring an absurd amount of scoring, playmaking and experience. The bench, with Anfernee Simons, Kentavious Caldwell-Pope and Dean Wade, may be a little underrated too.

So even if injuries cause them some problems along the way, Philadelphia should absolutely be in the championship mix.

After they won an unexpected 45 games in 2025-26, this feels like an overly harsh assessment of the Phoenix Suns.

They're not going to take as many opponents by surprise this season as they did last season. Two of the key players who made them a pleasant surprise are now gone.

Of course, if you could quantify talent, you could certainly argue that Miles Bridges and Luke Kennard would have more than Grayson Allen and Royce O'Neale. But last season's duo brought defensive grit and unselfishness on offense in ways that complemented the team.

Devin Booker should still be one of the 20-30 best players in the league. Dillon Brooks should help them maintain at least a lot of last season's attitude. That said, Phoenix ultimately had to be one of the casualties of the "there are only 1,230 wins available" rule.

In: Branden Carlson, Ja Morant, Micah Potter, Damian Lillard (back from injury)

Out: Matisse Thybulle, Jerami Grant, Kris Murray

The Portland Trail Blazers are another candidate for a step back in 2026-27 (at least in terms of wins and losses), but there's a fundamental difference between them and the Suns.

Devin Booker is now entering his 30s, being three full seasons removed from his career-high in offensive box plus/minus . Deni Avdija, on the other hand, turns 26 in January, made his first All-Star team last season and has increased his scoring average every year he's played in the NBA.

In other words, Portland's best player is ascending. Though he'll have to adjust to playing with ball-dominant guards Damian Lillard and Ja Morant, his two-way impact on a deeper roster should help the Blazers get to 42 wins again.

Rookies: Darius Acuff Jr., Alex Karaban, Emanuel Sharp

The Sacramento Kings are expected to be in the mix for the worst record in the West during the regular season.

What makes it a little easier to see them finishing lower than the Clippers is that, despite the new anti-tanking rules, Zach LaVine and Domantas Sabonis seem like two of the league's most likely trade candidates this season.

Without them, we'll have plenty of fun watching rookie Darius Acuff dominate the ball, but that won't lead to many wins this season.

Rookies: Jayden Quaintance, Tarris Reed Jr., Ja'Kobi Gillespie, Maliq Brown

These predictions have the Thunder finishing first in the West, but no one would be surprised to see the San Antonio Spurs in that spot.

All three of their best players—Victor Wembanyama, Dylan Harper and Stephon Castle—are several years away from their primes. All three should be better in 2026-27. The same could be said of Carter Bryant.

The only real difference in the veteran supporting cast is that Tobias Harris essentially replaces Kelly Olynyk, which should make the defense more switchable and the offense a little more dangerous off the bounce.

Barring injuries (always a concern with Wemby), this is a team that could absolutely be back in the Finals.

Out: Gradey Dick, Brandon Ingram, Sandro Mamukelashvili

The over-under on the Toronto Raptors has jumped by two full wins in the last couple of months. It's not hard to see why.

After Kawhi Leonard escaped the league's "Aspiration/cap circumvention" investigation, essentially, scot-free, Toronto and LA were allowed to complete the trade that reunited Kawhi with the Raptors.

With him in Brandon Ingram's spot and the rest of last season's most important players still in place, this team has a chance to be a real contender.

Leonard, Scottie Barnes and Collin Murray-Boyles will lead a potentially tenacious defense. Leonard's one-on-one scoring ability will take a ton of offensive pressure off Barnes and RJ Barrett.

The Utah Jazz are a trendy pick to pivot out of their rebuild and into play-in contention. Healthy seasons from Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr. could certainly get them there.

Utah is still depending heavily on young players who've never been on winning NBA teams. That's particularly true in the backcourt, where Keyonte George is still on his rookie contract (though he played like a vet last season) and Darryn Peterson is in his first campaign in the league.

The learning curve may be a little steeper than expected, especially if Markkanen and Jackson play as many games as they typically do. The former has averaged 54.7 appearances per season in his career, while the latter has averaged 56.9.

In: Deandre Ayton, Khris Middleton, Anthony Davis (back from injury)

Like the Jazz, the Washington Wizards should absolutely be better than they were last season.

Much has been said about their weaknesses in recent years, but Anthony Davis and Trae Young complement each other well. Having them around and commanding attention in the middle of the floor will accelerate Alex Sarr's development and soften AJ Dybantsa's landing in the league.

If one or two of the young guys, like Dybantsa or Tre Johnson, are better than expected, Washington might even threaten to finish above .500.

But Davis is one of the biggest injury risks in the league. Dybantsa, despite his immense talent, will experience NBA growing pains. High-end defense has long been tough to achieve when Young is on the floor.

articles.title: WNBA silent after Finals teams skip national anthem despite rule requiring players to stand and line up
articles.summary: The Dream and Valkyries have not explained their Game 1 anthem absences to OutKick, while the WNBA remains silent on enforcement and Game 2 expectations.
articles.body: SAN FRANCISCO – The WNBA’s own rulebook calls for players, coaches and trainers to stand and line up along the sidelines or foul line during the national anthem. Both of its Finals teams left the court for Saturday’s performance, and the league has not answered OutKick’s questions about their absences. And with Game 2 set for Monday night, neither team has told OutKick whether it plans to be on the floor for the anthem this time. GABBY WILLIAMS DELIVERS LATE AS VALKYRIES SHUT DOWN ANGEL REESE, DREAM TO WIN WNBA FINALS OPENER Both teams were warming up on the court Saturday at Chase Center before leaving just ahead of the national anthem. Within seconds of the performance ending, the players were jogging back onto the floor. Getting an explanation for why the teams chose to be off the floor for those roughly two minutes has been incredibly difficult. OutKick contacted the WNBA, and both the Dream and Valkyries on Saturday, then followed up with all three Sunday. None answered the anthem questions before publication. OutKick also attended all five of Saturday’s pregame and postgame press conferences but was not called on. We had planned to ask about the teams’ plans before the game and their absence from the anthem afterward. WNBA anthem enforcement and Game 2 plans remain unclear The follow-up questions to both teams were straightforward: Why were their players off the court during the Game 1 anthem? Would they be there for Game 2? Had the WNBA communicated any instructions or expectations about the anthem since Saturday? ANGEL REESE'S WNBA FINALS APPEARANCE AFTER CHICAGO EXIT RAISES QUESTIONS ABOUT WINNING MENTALITY The WNBA’s 2026 official rulebook includes an anthem provision covering players, coaches and trainers. It calls for them to form a standing line at a sideline or foul line while the anthem plays. The league has not answered OutKick’s questions about its anthem requirements, whether any discipline is planned or under consideration, or whether it will instruct either team to be present for Game 2. We also asked the league to confirm whether both teams would be on the court for Monday's anthem. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! If Saturday's absences were simply part of the teams' pregame routines, both have had an opportunity to explain that. Neither has done so in response to OutKick’s inquiries. But a pregame routine that keeps players off the floor during the national anthem deserves scrutiny. HOSTILE VALKYRIES FANS VERBALLY ATTACKED WOMEN'S SPORTS ACTIVISTS AT WNBA FINALS GAME 1 IN SAN FRANCISCO Game 2 is scheduled for 8 p.m. ET Monday at Chase Center. It took the teams mere seconds to return to the floor after the anthem. More than a day after OutKick asked why they left, the teams and the WNBA still haven’t answered.

articles.title: La maldición de Ben Simmons: se rompe el Aquiles cuando estaba a punto de volver a jugar tras año y medio
articles.standfirst: El jugador australiano de los Kings se perderá la temporada que está a punto de comenzar
articles.summary: El jugador australiano de los Kings se perderá la temporada que está a punto de comenzar
articles.body: La fama de jugador maldito sigue persiguiendo a Ben Simmons. No disputa un partido desde el 13 de abril de 2025. Estaba a punto de hacerlo. Y ahora que veía la luz al final del túnel, se produce un desprendimiento en la salida: se ha roto en el tendón de Aquiles de la pierna derecha. Será operado y, casi con total seguridad, se perderá toda la temporada que está a punto de arrancar. En veranos anteriores, las redes sociales se llenaban de vídeos de Simmons entrenando su tiro, ese que le ha martirizado durante toda su carrera en la NBA: un 13,9% de acierto con sólo 5/36 en 383 encuentros. Esta vez, sin necesidad de mostrar su mala mecánica, parecía listo para el regreso tras superar sus problemas físicos. A sus 30 años, los Kings le habían hecho un hueco en su plantilla y había ofrecido muy buenas sensaciones en el training camp. También en los dos amistosos jugados, en los que promedió 10,5 puntos en 17,5 minutos. No llegará a debutar en Liga regular. Una devastadora lesión durante un entrenamiento de cinco contra cinco supone un nuevo castigo para el jugador australiano. "Ya me he enfrentado a retos que me pusieron a prueba mental, física y emocionalmente, y he encontrado la manera de superarlos todos. Esta lesión es un capítulo más en mi camino, no el final de mi historia", ha explicado Simmons en un comunicado después de conocerse la lesión. "Nunca es fácil estar lejos del deporte que amo, especialmente después de todo lo que me costó volver aquí, pero si algo he aprendido es que la adversidad no te define. Lo que te define es cómo reaccionas ante ella", ha sentenciado el jugador. Simmons, número 1 del draft de 2016 elegido por los Sixers, ya se perdió su primera temporada en la NBA debido a una lesión en un pie. Tras el curso 2017-18 fue nombrado Rookie del Año tras promediar 15,8 puntos, 8,1 rebotes, 8,2 asistencias y 1,7 recuperaciones. Estando en Filadelfia, disputó tres veces el All Star y fue incluido en dos ocasiones en el mejor quinteto defensivo de la NBA. Su relación con los Sixers se deterioró hasta el extremo después de los playoffs de 2021. El equipo perdió en semifinales del Este y Simmons quedó marcado por algunas jugadas en las que renunciaba a lanzar. El entrenador Doc Rivers y la estrella Joel Embiid lanzaron críticas contra él. A la temporada siguiente, Simmons alegó problemas de salud mental y se ausentó de los entrenamientos. La franquicia le puso numerosas multas y fue suspendido en octubre de 2021. El curso 21-22 se lo perdió entero por esa rebelión y por problemas de espalda. Terminó siendo traspasado a los Nets, donde su realidad no mejoró demasiado. Los problemas físicos le persiguieron. Desde entonces, su máximo de partidos en una sola campaña son los 51 que disputó en la 24-25 entre la franquicia de Brooklyn y los Clippers, donde fue enviado. Su último encuentro fue en abril del año pasado. Estaba a punto de regresar a las canchas y vuelve a caer. Simmons está maldito.

articles.title: Bacanal de puntos del Real Madrid: el mejor inicio anotador en la historia de la ACB
articles.standfirst: Ningún equipo había metido 442 puntos (110,2 de media) en los primeros cuatro encuentros
articles.summary: Ningún equipo había metido 442 puntos (110,2 de media) en los primeros cuatro encuentros
articles.body: En la locura anotadora que está viviendo la Liga Endesa en este inicio de temporada, el Real Madrid ha establecido el récord histórico de puntos de la competición después de las cuatro primeras jornadas. Los blancos han sumado 442, con un bestial promedio de 110,5. La cifra supera el tope anterior, que estaba en poder del Barça desde la campaña 1985-86, cuando acumuló 437 puntos y una media de 109,3. El anterior récord anotador de los madridistas después de cuatro jornadas también databa de hace 41 años, cuando comenzaron el curso con 420 puntos y un promedio de 105,0. Ahora, han superado ese dato después de meter 89 al Unicaja en el estreno de la competición, 114 al Monbus Obradoiro después de una prórroga, 120 al Kids&Us Manresa y 119 este domingo al Surne Bilbao Basket. La mano de Pedro Martínez ya se deja notar en el conjunto madridista. El estilo que han llevado a cabo los últimos equipos del técnico se ha ido imponiendo: juego vertiginoso, con posesiones cortas y gran cantidad de triples. Desde hace un tiempo, los blancos marcan el ritmo de los encuentros también apoyados en su dominio del rebote. Después de estas primeras cuatro jornadas, el Madrid es el único equipo que queda invicto en la Liga Endesa. Marcha con un balance de 4-0 y, después de las palizas a los manresanos y los bilbaínos, un brillante average de +81. Es uno de sus mejores arranques en la historia de la ACB, aunque no el primero de la lista. En el ejercicio 2020-21, con Pablo Laso en el banquillo, también estaba inmaculado tras cuatro partidos y su average era de +83. La dinámica anotadora de los blancos también se ha trasladado a la Euroliga. En esta semana con doble jornada en la máxima competición continental, sumando los dos encuentros a los dos de ACB, el promedio se ha elevado hasta los 112,0 puntos después de meter 98 al Armani Milán y 111 al ASVEL Villeurbanne. El Madrid no es el único equipo de la Liga Endesa que está batiendo registros anotadores. El Río Breogán es el primero que supera los 100 puntos en las cuatro primeras jornadas y su total de 428 y su media de 107,0 también han entrado en el podio histórico sólo por detrás de las marcas de Real Madrid y Barcelona.

articles.title: WNBA Finals Goes Hollywood with ‘Orange Carpet’ Show
articles.summary: E! is bringing red carpet coverage to Game 2 of the Finals.
articles.body:
Game 2 of the WNBA Finals is getting some Hollywood flair thanks to E! and USA Network.

E! and USA Network, both Versant -owned channels, are teaming up to produce a one-hour, red carpet-style pregame show ahead of Game 2 on Monday night, marking the first time E! has extended its arrivals coverage beyond traditional entertainment events. Live from the Orange Carpet: WNBA Finals will air simultaneously on both channels beginning at 6 p.m. ET.

A live panel featuring comedian Wanda Sykes, WNBA legend Tina Thompson, and WNBA player stylist Brittany Hampton will anchor the special. Canadian actress Lilly Singh—who joined the Toronto Tempo ownership group last year—will host.

"We're now the pre-pre-show, so we'll talk about a lot of fun things—the culture, the personalities, the looks," Singh told Front Office Sports . E!'s usual red carpet shows are famous for their "glam cams" that document attendees' hair, makeup, and outfits. The WNBA "has a lot of really heavy hitters when it comes to fashion," Singh said. "Not only are women amazing athletes, but we also serve looks, and I'm so excited to spotlight that."

The WNBA first rolled out its orange carpet during All-Star Weekend in 2022 to give players a chance to showcase their personal style, and it has since become a fixture of the league's draft night. Monday night's show takes the concept a step further.

It's a fitting treatment for a series that features Angel Reese—a known fashionista and the league's most-followed player on social media—as well as the Valkyries, which lead the WNBA in nearly every major business metric, from ticket sales to overall valuation. (Plus, Valkyries fans have embraced the team's violet colors with enough enthusiasm to become style icons in their own right.) But Christian McLaughlin, Versant's SVP of live entertainment, told FOS that Live from the Orange Carpet was in the works "well before" the Finals matchup was set.

Singh aims to reach a wide audience with the show, but also hopes it signals a shift for long-time WNBA fans. "For the fans that have been watching for years and years, I want this to feel like 'Oh, the way the sport is being packaged is evolving.' Now there's a pre-show, and a pre-pre-show, and a panel—all these things that maybe didn't exist not that long ago," she said. "There's more programming and more commentary than ever. This is just the latest proof that the way [the WNBA] is being talked about has evolved."

If there was ever a time to experiment with WNBA programming, it's now. The league continues to grow its ratings and attendance; the first round of the playoffs delivered record viewership .

The Valkyries took a 1–0 lead in the Finals, beating the Dream 68–64 on Saturday. Game 2 tips off at 8 p.m. ET Monday, after the Orange Carpet and WNBA on USA pregame shows at 6 p.m. ET and 7 p.m. ET, respectively.

If the special is a success, more crossover programming could be on the way across Versant properties..

"The key is finding the right moments—where the energy, personalities and culture around a sport lend themselves to a fun, live experience that feels authentic to both audiences," McLaughlin told FOS . "We'll continue looking for similar opportunities across our portfolio."

articles.title: Trey Kaufman-Renn Commits to Kansas, Ex-Purdue Big Man Was Drafted by Timberwolves in 2026
articles.summary: Kansas announced Monday it signed former Purdue star Trey Kaufman-Renn ahead of the 2026-27 men's basketball season.
articles.body:
Kansas announced Monday it signed former Purdue star Trey Kaufman-Renn ahead of the 2026-27 men's basketball season.

"Trey Kaufman-Renn, who had a tremendous career at Purdue, has enrolled in classes, and is practicing with us as of Sunday," head coach Bill Self said . "He reached the national championship game, the Elite Eight and the Sweet 16 at Purdue and has been extremely well-drilled and well-coached. Even though it's late in the process, because of his basketball IQ, we think his transition will be quicker than most put in the same circumstance."

The Minnesota Timberwolves selected Kaufman-Renn in the second round of the 2026 NBA draft. He won a preliminary injunction earlier this month that opened the door for him to receive one more year of college eligibility.

The Jayhawks said the 6'9" forward will replace true freshman Grant Mordini, who will be sidelined for the entire season because of a patellar injury. Going from Mordini to Kaufman-Renn would be a massive upgrade to the frontcourt.

In his final two seasons with the Boilermakers, Kaufman-Renn averaged 17.1 points on 58.7 percent shooting along with 7.4 rebounds and 2.4 assists. He was a first-team All-Big Ten honoree for 2024-25 and then merited selection on the All-Region team in the 2026 NCAA tournament.

Kaufman-Renn's legal saga isn't over, however, so it remains to be seen how much — if at all — he'll suit up for Kansas. The NCAA could appeal the injunction, a step that would cast renewed uncertainty over his eligibility.

Tre White and Melvin Council Jr. are in the same boat after having returned to the Jayhawks.

Assuming all three of the experienced transfers are cleared, Self will have a formidable squad. White and Council will provide experience and continuity alongside Tyran Stokes , the No. 1 overall player in 247Sports' composite rankings for 2026.

Kansas opens the regular season on Nov. 2 against Fordham.

articles.title: New NBA Trade Rumors on Cavs' Evan Mobley, Lakers' Knecht, Knicks' Kolek amid Roster Deadline

articles.body:
The start of the 2026-27 NBA season is just over 24 hours away, and trade rumors are already starting to swirl.

ESPN's Brian Windhorst reported that Cleveland Cavaliers star forward Evan Mobley is expected to be safe after the team chose not to include him in offers for stars like Giannis Antetokounmpo and Jaylen Brown earlier this offseason.

"The front office still deeply believes in Mobley in the wake of a bit of a disappointing season," Windhorst stated.

NBA Stars with Most on the Line This Season 🫡

The Cavs instead opted to acquire Peyton Watson from the Denver Nuggets, which "caused them to make a series of expensive trades and salary shedding moves" because they "believe Watson is on the verge of a breakout after he showed flashes in Denver last season," Windhorst explained.

Meanwhile, the Los Angeles Lakers are reportedly shopping 2024 first-round pick Dalton Knecht ahead of Monday's deadline to cut down their roster from 16 guaranteed contracts to 15.

NBA insider Marc Stein reported that the team "spent the weekend trying to find a workable trade" for the 25-year-old that would "maybe even bring back a big man — such as Milwaukee's Jericho Sims." However, Stein added, "If no trade can be found, they'll have to waive Knecht (or someone else) by the cut-down buzzer."

Stein also revealed that 2024 second-round pick Tyler Kolek isn't in jeopardy with the New York Knicks, as they "did not shop [him] to try to make roster room for Bruce Brown before Brown's release Saturday." The Golden State Warriors are facing an uphill battle as they start the 2026-27 season with a litany of injuries to key players.

articles.title: Fantasy Basketball 2026 Deep NBA Sleepers After Preseason
articles.summary: We made it.
articles.body:
After an unpredictable offseason and an appetite-whetting preseason, the 2026-27 NBA season is here in all of its glory.

The new campaign tips off Tuesday night, and it will soon carry all kinds of revelations. Like any changes to the league's constellation of stars amid the latest round of player movement. Or any differences to the balance of power from said movement or the growth and decline attached to everyone's aging curve.

On a lesser note for many—but of perhaps maximum importance to fantasy basketballers—it will also shed light on which, if any, preseason darlings might carry over that success and deliver on the fantasy-sleeper potential they've shown so far. These are three deep sleepers holding our attention.

The Magic are in a tricky spot where they are attempting to change their fortune with mostly the same roster in place. While there are obviously hopes tied to new head coach Sean Sweeney, there are surely also fingers-crossed for some positive internal developments within this group.

If the preseason was any indication, maybe third-year forward Tristan da Silva has a leap year brewing.

He netted the second-most points on the team (16.5) and generally lived up to his jack-of-all-trades billing by touching every inch of the box score. In four games, he also tallied 3.8 rebounds, 2.8 assists and 1.3 stocks in just 21.6 minutes.

Perhaps most importantly, he showed both volume (3.5 threes per game) and efficiency (37.8 percent) with his outside shot, which could be his key to upping his playing time with a Magic team that has been perennially squeezed for spacing.

When a rookie enters the NBA, it's never entirely clear which of their skills will translate to the big stage. That said, they'll always have their size and length with them, and if it's the kind that makes them an interior deterrent, that's the kind of trait that has a better conversion rate than most.

That, in a nutshell, is a reason to keep all eyes glued on Aday Mara, who posted eye-popping measurements at the Combine (7'3" barefoot with a 7'6" wingspan) and eye-popping preseason production to go along with it.

Over five outings, Mara managed to pack 13.4 points, 7.6 rebounds, 2.8 assists and 2.4 blocks into just 23.3 minutes a night. He also shot 78.8 percent from the field and 78.9 percent at the line, meaning he could be a big helper in categories that can drag down other shot-blocking specialists.

Mara still carries fairly significant fantasy risk, though it's related to his possible role and not his readiness. OKC is overloaded in the frontcourt with Chet Holmgren, Isaiah Hartenstein, Jaylin Williams and Thomas Sorber all also capable of manning the middle. That said, talent typically finds a way to work these things out, so if the Thunder believe Mara is as good as he looked in exhibitions, they'll figure out how to find him floor time.

Assuming that whatever shelved Jarace Walker for the Indiana Pacers' final two preseason games doesn't carry over into the actual campaign, the fourth-year forward and No. 8 pick of the 2023 draft might be engineering a breakout.

Granted, that's borderline reckless to say after just two preseason appearances, but man, those outings were fun.

He posted per-game averages of 8.5 points, 6.5 assists and 6.0 rebounds, highlighting his unique blend of size, strength and skill. He also posted encouraging shooting percentages from the field (46.2) and from three (42.9).

Consistency has been a challenge so far, though that applies both to production and role. It hasn't been easy to ace his assignments when the questions have changed so often. Stability in expectations could go a long way toward maximizing his potential.

And he also has some urgency to make that happen, since, barring an unlikely extension, this will be a contract year for him. Should the stars align, he could be an all-categories kind of producer.

Cleveland, Detroit, Miami y Boston buscarán un puesto en las Finales de conferencia y quién sabe si en la final de la NBA, mientras Indiana y Washington podrían ser dos de los equipos más mejorados de la temporada. Los Atlanta Hawks vivirán su primera temporada completa tras el traspaso del que ha sido su gran estrella en el pasado, Trae Young. Se han sumergido en el mercado para potenciar su banquillo, con jugadores como Aaron Wiggins, Luguentz Dort y Dorian Finney-Smith, todos ellos con probada experiencia en la Liga, y sobre todo han logrado retener a CJ McCollum, que será su referente y su guía esta temporada. Las expectativas son altas en los Hawks porque sienten que acuden a la Liga regular con mejores mimbres que otros años a pesar del traspaso en enero de Young y de haber soltado a su número 1 del 2024, Zaccharie Risacher. Eso sí, no será nada fácil repetir el sexto puesto (46-36) del año pasado para caer en primera ronda con los Knicks (4-2). Renovaciones: Jock Landale (un año) y CJ McCollum (un año). Por Brown obtienen a Paul George y varias elecciones de Draft. De George no se espera un milagro en Boston y menos con sus problemas físicos eternos, de las elecciones de Draft se consideran un tesoro de cara al futuro a corto y medio plazo. Para eso han traído de nuevo a Nueva York a Julius Randle, aunque al equipo vecino, que formará una extraordinaria dupla ofensiva con Michael Porter. Jordi Fernández está ante un enorme reto. Debe desarrollar el talento de jugadores como Egor Demin y el excitante novato Michael Brown Jr. y mezclarlo con veteranos como Randle, Porter o el recién llegado Wagner para conseguir la química que necesita un equipo que tiene que luchar por meterse en el Play-In. articles.title: Men's college basketball preseason AP poll: Florida edges Duke to start year at No. 1 for the first time in decades
articles.summary: The Gators last started the season as the top team in the country in 2006, when they were fresh off their first of back-to-back national titles.
articles.body:
Florida, for the first time in two decades, is starting the season on top.

The Gators were named the No. 1 team in the country in the Associated Press preseason Top 25 poll on Monday, just two weeks before the 2026-27 college basketball season kicks off.

It marks Florida's first time atop the preseason poll since 2006 and makes the Gators the early favorite to win what would be a second national championship in three seasons. The last time they opened at No. 1 in this poll was fresh off the first of what ended up being back-to-back titles.

Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Basketball league for the 2026-27 NBA season

And, just like it was two decades ago, Florida is bringing back a significant chunk of its roster from last year's group that earned a top seed in the NCAA tournament. Thomas Haugh, who was widely projected to be a lottery pick, opted to skip the NBA Draft and return for one more season in what was a huge get for Todd Golden. He was joined by Alex Condon and starting center Reuben Chinyelu, who was the national Defensive Player of the Year. But the biggest boost perhaps comes from Denzel Aberdeen.

Aberdeen transferred in to play for Golden again this past spring from Kentucky, and earned a temporary injunction last month to be able to play a fifth season. Aberdeen was on Florida's national title team in 2025, too, so he knows the system well. The roster, especially with Aberdeen around, is deep.

But Duke is in a similar spot after just barely missing out on a trip to the Final Four last spring. Caleb Foster is coming back, and Jon Scheyer landed former Wisconsin star John Blackwell in the transfer market. Cayden Boozer and Pat Ngongba are back, and Duke is bringing in star freshman Joaquim Boumtje Boumtje and Cam Williams, who are the fourth- and fifth-ranked players in their recruiting class .

Scheyer has plenty of options at any given time, though Duke's run through the ACC won't be as easy as it has been in recent years. The league has five teams ranked in the preseason poll, including No. 9 Virginia, No. 11 Louisville and No. 14 Miami.

Illinois came in at No. 3, UConn will start at No. 4, and Arizona rounds out the top five.

Now, a lot is going to change over the next several months. The last team who opened the season in the top spot and then went on to win the national championship was North Carolina during the 2008-09 campaign. Purdue was the No. 1 team at this point last season, and the Boilermakers fell shy of making the Final Four.

But at least to start, Florida is leading the way.

What about the defending national champions?

Michigan is fresh off its first national championship in decades, though the program has gone through a lot of changes in the months since.

Perhaps most importantly, head coach Dusty May jumped ship for the Dallas Mavericks in the NBA. He did so just before the NBA Draft, too, forcing the Wolverines to make a very late switch at the top. Michigan has since promoted assistant and former Oklahoma State head coach Mike Boynton to replace him.

Then last month, Michigan announced that star freshman Brandon McCoy Jr. would miss the entire 2026-27 season after he went down with an ACL injury in their exhibition game with Mega Superbet in Europe. McCoy, a five-star Rivals recruit, went down just 20 seconds into that contest.

It's not all bad news, though. Boynton is an experienced head coach who was on staff for their title run, and the Wolverines get Elliot Cadeau back. He averaged 10.5 points and 5.9 assists per game, but is the lone starter returning from their championship team. Kenny Noland has transferred in from Columbia, too, and Roddy Gayle Jr. is currently trying to earn a fifth year of eligibility. If Gayle is granted that and comes out on top of his legal battle, it would be a huge boost for the Wolverines.

Michigan will start out at No. 16 in the first poll. It'll open the year against Oakland on Nov. 2 before a contest with UConn in Boston just days later.

While things haven't been completely reset in Ann Arbor, this is far from the same group that won the national title last April.

articles.title: AP College Basketball Poll 2026 Preseason Men's Rankings Released
articles.summary: Florida sits atop the Associated Press Top 25 poll as it looks to collect a second national title in three seasons in men's basketball.
articles.body:
Florida sits atop the Associated Press Top 25 poll as it looks to collect a second national title in three seasons in men's basketball.

The Gators received 47 first-place votes to beat out Duke for the No. 1 spot.

Michigan, the reigning champion, is down in 16th. The Wolverines' three leading scorers (Yaxel Lendeborg, Morez Johnson and Aday Mara) all left for the NBA, and coach Dusty May did the same. As a result, they face plenty of questions.

The general expectations around Florida couldn't be much higher. The Gators return Thomas Haugh, Alex Condon, Boogie Fland and Rueben Chinyelu, and they received an added boost when 2025 national champion Denzel Aberdeen was deemed eligible to play a fifth season.

It's increasingly rare, especially in college basketball, for a team to have this much talent and continuity return.

Florida's status as the top dog will be put to the test early as the Gators will host Duke on Dec. 1.

Blue Devils coach Jon Scheyer and his staff cleaned up on the recruiting trail. They had the second-best class in 247Sports' composite rankings , and the group includes four top-30 prospects: Cameron Williams, Deron Rippey Jr., Bryson Howard and Joaquim Boumtje Boumtje.

Despite losing national player of the year Cameron Boozer, Duke has the pieces for another trip to the Final Four.

In 2025-26, Kentucky was a primary example of how an NIL payroll isn't directly correlated to a team's success. The Wildcats reportedly spent north of $20 million to go 21-13 in the regular season and lose in the second round of the NCAA tournament.

St. John's and Louisville will both try to avoid a similar fate after making a lot of noise in the transfer portal.

In the case of the Red Storm, they were left in limbo over the status of Keyshawn Hall, Quinn Ellis and Babacar Sane. The Cardinals were in the same spot with Seth Trimble and LJ Wells but at least had more certainty with their two biggest transfer additions, Flory Bidunga and Jackson Shelstad.

Trying to rank the 25 best teams in a preseason poll is always difficult because nobody has a peek into the future. The task becomes even more challenging when you can't even be assured of who will be playing where on opening night.

articles.title: Inside LeBron, Nick Nurse's Phone Call from Golf Course to Sell James on 76ers in NBA Free Agency
articles.summary: Over the summer, Philadelphia 76ers head coach Nick Nurse was at the Carroll National Golf Club in Iowa, which he owns, when he received a phone call from then-free agent LeBron James.
articles.body:
Over the summer, Philadelphia 76ers head coach Nick Nurse was at the Carroll National Golf Club in Iowa, which he owns, when he received a phone call from then-free agent LeBron James.

According to Brendan Quinn of The Athletic, "James, in the midst of the summer's most closely followed free agency bonanza, told Nurse he had some questions; an effort, he said, to do his due diligence. James asked about offensive roles, defensive roles, team schemes, how he might fit. The greatest player of this generation wanted to know how Nurse might use the greatest player of this generation. ... What Nurse told LeBron, we can't be totally sure, but it seems like it ultimately helped. At minimum, it didn't hurt."

The rest is history. James signed a veteran minimum deal with the Sixers, joining Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey, VJ Edgecombe and Jaylen Brown to form arguably the most talented roster in the NBA, at least on paper.

How it will all play out remains to be seen. James is expected to operate as the team's primary playmaker in more of a point-forward role, and there are plenty of mouths to feed in Philadelphia.

But if it all works, the Sixers could finally end a title drought dating back to the 1982-83 season.

articles.body: Salvo que equipos como los Nuggets, los Wolves, los Rockets o, en menor medida los Lakers, arrojen algunas dudas, todo parece indicar que la Conferencia Oeste camina hacia una nueva final entre los Spurs y los Thunder. Y en esa pelea, parten con ventaja los tejanos que han reforzado su extraordinaria plantilla, la que jugó las Finales de la NBA, con Tobias Harris mientras que los de Oklahoma siguen buscando el equilibrio entre ahorro y competitividad. A San Antonio les llegaron las Finales antes de tiempo, pero 2027 puede ser ya su momento. Su líder, Victor Wembanyama, podría incluso convertirse en el quinto jugador no estadounidense en ganar el MVP de forma consecutiva. Aunque hubo algunos cambios en la plantilla, con la marcha de Klay Thompson o la llegada de Santi Aldama, las mayores novedades de los Mavs estuvieron en su despacho. La adquisición de Masai Ujiri brinda al equipo la figura del arquitecto del título de los Toronto Raptors de 2019. Y su primera decisión fue prescindir de Jason Kidd y fichar aire muy fresco en Dusty May, ex entrenador de los Michigan Wolverines campeones de la NCAA. Los Mavs de este año tendrán enorme presencia española con Santi Aldama, un veterano del que se espera impacto inmediato como con Marcus Sasser, y con Sergio de Larrea, que puede tener mucha presencia en pista. El veterano base seguirá siendo el jugador en el que descanse el proyecto, ayudado por otros veteranos como Jimmy Butler, Al Horford, Draymond Green y Kristaps Porzingis. Eso sí, lograron proteger sus elecciones de Draft del futuro y tendrán pronto espacio en el límite salarial. Pero en lo que se refiere al presente, el equipo tratará de mejorar las 37 victorias del año pasado para intentar no pasar por el filtro del Play-In. articles.title: Enes Kanter Freedom Says He Will Attend WNBA Finals Game 3 in Atlanta
articles.summary: ATLANTA (AP) — Former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom announced on social media that he plans to attend Game 3 of the WNBA Finals in Atlanta on Wednesday as a fan.
articles.body:
ATLANTA (AP) — Former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom announced on social media that he plans to attend Game 3 of the WNBA Finals in Atlanta on Wednesday as a fan.

Freedom last was at a WNBA game in late August when he went to see Chicago host Indiana. He was ejected from the game and banned from the arena for getting into a heated interaction with Sky guard Natasha Cloud.

"As you all know, this all started with an interview featuring Gabby Williams of the Golden State Valkyries, when she said, 'I have no problem with trans athletes playing on my team or against my team.' Her words gave me so much hope and motivation to come out as a woman and officially declare for the WNBA Draft. I can't wait to watch my favorite player, the woman who inspired me to become who I am today!" Freedom said in his post.

The league declined to comment on Freedom potentially attending the Finals.

Freedom and Royce White, another former NBA player, have declared for the WNBA draft, saying they identify as women. But a person familiar with the decision told The Associated Press in August they are not eligible .

The WNBA has been the subject of recent debates on whether transgender women — people assigned male at birth who transition to align with their gender identity — should be allowed to participate in the league. There has never been such a player in the WNBA.

Although the league's collective bargaining agreement says the WNBA is restricted to women, it contains no more specific language about gender identity or sex assigned at birth.

The Charlotte Hornets' offseason trade of LaMelo Ball signaled a few things.

The Hornets may simply have valued him a bit less than the Minnesota Timberwolves did. Charlotte may not have been confident that he'd have another season as healthy as 2025-26. It might be higher on Coby White than people realize.

The biggest takeaway, though, is that the organization does have plenty of confidence in Kon Knueppel and Brandon Miller to be its two best players. And with that being the case, an extension for Miller, even at a pretty lofty price, wouldn't be surprising.

He's had his own struggles with availability, but over the last two seasons, Miller has averaged 20.4 points, 3.4 assists and 3.e threes in 31.4 minutes, while shooting 37.3 percent from deep.

At 6'7", he has good size for a wing and is only 23 years old.

This season, he should get a chance to expand on his playmaking duties a bit. And the Hornets should be eager to lock in his longterm salary before a further breakout forces it to max territory.

articles.title: Amari Williams: Boston Celtics’ British big man ‘ready’ for Detroit reunion after career-defining moment
articles.summary: Amari Williams is on a two-way contract and wants to follow team-mates Luka Garza and Neemias Queta's lead by securing his long-term future; watch the Boston Celtics open the 2026-27 NBA season at the Detroit Pistons, live on Sky Sports Mix from 8pm on Tuesday 20 October
articles.body:
Williams' two-way contract allows him to feature for both Boston and the Maine Celtics, the NBA franchise's development affiliate in the G-League.

His Celtics team-mate Luka Garza was the 52nd pick out of 60 in the 2021 draft, and earned a standard NBA contract by way of a two-way deal at Minnesota. Fellow centre Neemias Queta went 39th in the same draft, arrived in Boston on a two-way and was promoted to a multi-year standard contract in April 2024. In July, he signed a four-year extension worth $56m (£42.3m) that runs to 2031.

Now the challenge is for Williams to follow suit and make his place in the NBA permanent, with his first opportunity coming when Boston face the Detroit Pistons in their opening game on Tuesday, live on Sky Sports from 8pm.

The Brit was the 46th pick in the 2025 draft and has already experienced that first promotion. Boston converted his original two-way deal into a standard NBA contract in February, only for the 24-year-old to return to a two-way arrangement in July.

The Nottingham centre, the first British-born player in Celtics history, has been studying both Garza and Queta.

"[Garza and Queta] have been there before me. They both started on the two-way and they've taken me under their wing, always giving me words of encouragement or telling me what to do in situations," Williams exclusively told Sky Sports.

"Having guys like that who care about me and help me any way they can has definitely helped me a lot over the past year."

Williams has already proved he can make an impact at NBA level, with his most significant moment coming against the same opponent Boston faces on opening night .

Last November, the centre was brought up from Maine without warning and played a career-high 15 minutes against a Detroit team riding a franchise record-equalling 13-game winning streak.

With 4.4 seconds left and Boston a point up, Pistons superstar Cade Cunningham missed a free throw that would have tied the game. Williams got the first hand on the ball and tipped it to Payton Pritchard, who gathered the rebound before making two free throws at the other end.

Detroit's 13-game winning streak was over.

"I didn't have any idea I was gonna play, to be honest," Williams told CelticsBlog afterwards.

Williams, who represented Great Britain in EuroBasket pre-qualifiers in August, knows opportunities can arrive without warning.

"With those things it's never determined. There's always opportunities available and whether they call you up or not, you just got to be ready for that moment," he said.

Williams faces considerable competition for minutes in Boston, who have acquired significant reinforcement in his position over the summer.

Mitchell Robinson arrived from NBA champions New York on a three-year deal worth $47.4m to share the middle with Queta, while Garza started Game 7 of Boston's first-round playoff defeat by Philadelphia.

Chris Cenac Jr, a 6ft 11in forward and center, was the 27th pick in June's draft.

"To be honest, it's just about learning from those guys," Williams said. "I feel like I've got a great set of bigs ahead of me who are experienced in the league and have had the same kind of pathway as me.

"I look up to all those guys. All those guys are older than me, more experienced.

"So I'm not really sure about the impact part, but for me it's just about learning and being ready for opportunity when it comes."

Jayson Tatum and Paul George can both operate at power forward, with Sam Hauser and Jordan Walsh also competing for minutes. Dillon Mitchell provides another option on a two-way contract.

Williams will likely need to impress for Maine again to earn further opportunities with Boston, but Queta offers proof that patience can pay off.

The Portuguese centre spent two seasons on the bench for the Celtics before starting 75 of his 76 appearances last term, averaging 10.2 points and 8.4 rebounds while shooting a franchise-record 65.3 per cent from the field.

He was in contention for the Most Improved Player award for his performances in what was his fifth NBA season.

Williams has a skillset that distinguishes him from many players of his size.

Across 28 G League games he averaged 15.8 points, 10.9 rebounds, 4.9 assists and 1.8 blocks in a little over 29 minutes a night.

The assist number stands out. Almost five a game from a 6ft 11in center is an impressive return and helps explain why Boston have highlighted his passing ability.

He has produced standout individual performances, too.

On January 3, Williams scored 33 points and grabbed 16 rebounds against Capital City. A month later, he hit an overtime game-winner at Sioux Falls.

Through his first 23 G League appearances, he scores at an impressive 61.3 per cent from the field - well above average for players in his position.

He carried that form into the summer, scoring a game-high 23 points from nine field-goal attempts, alongside 13 rebounds and two blocks, in Boston's Summer League opening victory over Toronto.

"We won that game, and it was a very close game, we won in overtime," he said. "So having that game gave us that confidence, and it being the first one, it definitely set the tone for the rest of the games for us.

"I feel like it went well. We had a good record – I think it was three and one. So to have a winning record again is something we kind of took pride in."

Nottingham, Drexel and a family decision

Williams' route to the NBA was unusual, especially for a British player.

He left Nottingham at 16 and spent four seasons at Drexel University, where he was named Colonial Athletic Association Defensive Player of the Year three times between 2022 and 2024.

He then moved to Kentucky, starting all 36 games and averaging 10.9 points, 8.5 rebounds, 3.2 assists and 1.2 blocks.

He also finished with more assists than any seven-footer in the programme's history, according to Boston's official account of his college career.

The Nottingham Forest fan remains proud of his roots and the basketball community that helped him develop.

"I feel like Nottingham is an underrated city," he said. "We have the Wildcats arena, which is essentially for the women's league. We have the Nottingham Hoods. We had teams around, and at the time we had Nottingham Nova, that's who I started playing for.

"It was one of the best teams for a while, always a top four in the country. Having that around me when I was growing up, it was easy to get into the game and have guys who I looked up to and inspired me to play.

"Once it came to my age groups, I felt like I was one of the better players in the country, and it just took off from there."

Williams has already made the journey from Nottingham to the NBA and from a two-way contract to a standard deal.

As Boston begin their new campaign against Detroit, the next challenge is to establish himself there for good.

articles.title: Steph Curry Injury Update, Latest on Warriors Star's Status Ahead of NBA Opener vs. Lakers
articles.summary: Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry will play in Wednesday's season opener against the Los Angeles Lakers after suffering an ankle injury during the team's open practice on Sunday, head coach Steve Kerr told reporters on Monday.
articles.body:
Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry will play in Wednesday's season opener against the Los Angeles Lakers after suffering an ankle injury during the team's open practice on Sunday, head coach Steve Kerr told reporters on Monday.

According to the Warriors , Curry suffered a right ankle sprain.

Curry, 38, is heading into his 18th season with the Warriors on an expiring $62 million contract.

He was available for just half of the 2025-26 campaign due to ankle, quadricep and knee injuries.

That included an issue Curry described as "runner's knee," which sidelined him for two months between February and April.

When available last season, Curry averaged 26.6 points on 46.8 percent shooting from the field and 39.3 shooting from deep.

He added 3.6 rebounds, 4.7 assists and 1.1 steals per game while playing 30.9 minutes per night in 43 games.

Curry's absence had a major impact on his team's success, especially when he missed time while Jimmy Butler was already sidelined with a knee injury.

The Warriors went 13-26 without Curry in the lineup and 24-19 with him playing. Curry ultimately returned in time for last spring's play-in tournament but was unable to will his team to victory over the Phoenix Suns.

As Butler continues recovering from the surgical repair of his torn right ACL he underwent in January, having Curry in the lineup will be crucial to the Warriors' hopes of staying in postseason contention.

Should Curry ultimately miss any time, Draymond Green could be tasked with increasing his offensive production as Brandin Podziemski and De'Anthony Melton see more playing time in the backcourt.
